stories.title: Hornets, Brandon Miller agree to 5-year, $209M rookie extension
stories.summary: The Hornets and forward Brandon Miller agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension.
stories.detailText: Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller has agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension, representatives AJ Vaynerchuk and Joey Middleton of VaynerSports told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Miller, who turns 24 next month, had a career season last year, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 38.3% shooting from 3 in 65 regular-season games. He was also able to stay mostly healthy following a season in which he appeared in just 27 games. Miller, along with then-rookie Kon Knueppel , helped spearhead a surprise run to the postseason in the second half of last year, where they fell in the second play-in game. He was especially key to Charlotte's midseason turnaround, as the Hornets went 41-24 with Miller available and 3-14 without him. He missed a chunk of the beginning of the season due to a shoulder injury. Miller underwent surgery in May to address the stability of that shoulder but he has since fully recovered and appeared in preseason for Charlotte. Heading into his fourth year in the league, Miller will be stepping into an even bigger role for the Hornets this season after the team traded away longtime franchise staples LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges . The Hornets drafted Miller with the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

stories.title: Lakers make final roster decision, waive Dalton Knecht as Bronny stays
stories.summary: Why Dalton Knecht's release felt inevitable as the preseason came to a close. Here's what we know about Lakers final roster move.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers have come to a decision on their roster to open the season. Dalton Knecht has been waived, the team announced Monday afternoon. The move puts the Lakers roster at 15 players, the limit under NBA rules. The Lakers, who carried 16 players through the preseason, had a choice to make between Knecht and Bronny James. Both players were held out of practice ahead of Monday's 2 p.m. cut deadline, with head coach JJ Redick saying the two cut candidates were "under the weather." And despite rumors over the weekend of trade talks centered around Knecht, it appears president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka ultimately decided to make a clean break. Lakers waive Dalton Knecht The problem that comes with trading a player who won't make the roster comes down to value. Teams have no reason to give up any assets for a guy they know they can get for nothing a few days later. Pelinka has shown over the years that he's particular about return packages; he's more than willing to pass on a trade if he's not 100% sure it would improve the roster. For Knecht, it became painfully clear over the last couple of weeks that he was the odd man out . His shooting -- the reason the Lakers drafted him with the 17th overall pick in 2024 in the first place -- was too streaky to be relied upon, and his subpar defense made him a liability most times he stepped on the court. That, and the addition of several wings with size who could shoot -- Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili when he's not playing the five -- during their roster overhaul this summer, suddenly made Knecht's skillset redundant. Redick admitted as much to reporters ahead of Friday's preseason finale. "I think the biggest thing is the team changed. The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he’s gotten better as a player the last two years. I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings," Redick said at the time. "And he’s in a tough spot right now." Knecht didn't check in until halfway through the fourth quarter of the Lakers' loss to the Denver Nuggets, the 12th man off the bench that night, and finished scoreless for the second game in a row. In his 7:30 minutes of playing time, he added one rebound and an assist. The writing had been on the wall at UCLA Health Training Center for quite some time. Now, it's official. Oct. 16 Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions. Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge. For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET. Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama , Amen and Ausar Thompson , Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023. Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace . Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility. The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks Read more: Which NBA deals will get done? Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious. "The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape." The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws. "For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm." Doncic badly strained his hamstring in early April and missed the entire Lakers playoff run while rehabbing the injury. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." stories.title: Hornets, Brandon Miller reportedly agree to $209M contract extension ahead of Monday's deadline
stories.summary: The two sides agreed to the deal Monday, hours ahead of a deadline for players from Miller’s draft class to sign an extension.
stories.detailText: The Charlotte Hornets and Brandon Miller have agreed to a five-year, $209 million extension to his rookie contract, ESPN’s Shams Charania reports — a deal cementing the No. 2 overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft as one of the cornerstones of the ongoing effort to build a consistent contender in the Queen City. The two sides agreed to the deal Monday, hours ahead of a deadline for players from Miller’s draft class to sign an extension. Had they not reached agreement on a deal, Miller would have played the upcoming season on a team option, then gone into next offseason as a restricted free agent. Instead, Miller is under contract for five more seasons at $41.8 million per year after playing the first four seasons of his rookie contract for a total of $49.4 million. The former Alabama standout bounced back from an injury-wracked sophomore season to turn in a stellar third campaign, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.3 minutes per game with a career-best .574 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy). Miller was one of only a dozen wing players to hit those marks last season, according to Stathead ; 10 of the other 11 members of the list are All-Star and All-NBA honorees. (We see you, Trey Murphy III.) The list of wings to produce like that by their age-23 season includes some of the brightest young perimeter players in the league in recent years — names like Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Durant, James Harden, Jayson Tatum, Anthony Edwards, Devin Booker and Jalen Williams. That's the kind of company that the Hornets are betting — and betting big — that Miller can continue to keep, developing into the kind of perennial All-Star and All-NBA candidate who can lift Charlotte into the ranks of the league's elite teams. After missing most of the first month of the season following a left shoulder subluxation , Miller played a significant role in helping the Hornets climb out of an early hole to become one of the hottest teams in the NBA over the final few months. LaMelo Ball's high-octane playmaking and rookie Kon Knueppel's deadeye marksmanship drew the most headlines, but the 6-foot-7 Miller's all-around play on the wing — as a spot-up threat on the weak side of the primary action, as a complementary pick-and-roll ball-handler, as a speed demon sprinting the floor in transition, and as an improved multipositional perimeter defender — helped tie it all together for head coach Charles Lee's squad, which boasted the NBA's sixth-best record and second -best net rating after Christmas, according to Cleaning the Glass . "Definitely [want to do] everything I can do to win a basketball game, whether that's guarding the best player, guarding a player that can't shoot or [has a] lower percentage, I take pride in that two-way mindset," Miller told Rod Boone of the Charlotte Observer last season . "It's been going great this year. We get a lot of wins when everybody's locked into that two-way mindset. So, just keep having that mindset." That second-half surge led the Hornets to the verge of the postseason, with a play-in victory over the Miami Heat followed by a loss to the Orlando Magic in their second play-in contest. But despite coming within arm's reach of the franchise's first playoff appearance since 2016 , and despite playing the most exciting and energizing brand of ball that Hornets fans have seen in ages, Charlotte's brass elected to reorient the roster this summer, dealing Ball and guard Josh Green to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for sweet-shooting forward Naz Reid, an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, swap rights on Minnesota's firsts in 2028, 2029 and 2030, and second-round picks in 2029, 2032 and 2033. Whatever rationale you ascribe to the trade — the Hornets' front office not believing the roster was quite as good as that torrid second half suggested, seizing the opportunity to get out of the Ball business after he'd had a healthy season for the first time in four years, believing Coby White could replace most of Ball's production at a substantially lower dollar figure, etc. — it also represented, to some degree, a bet on Miller (and Knueppel) being able to expand his offensive game and shot-creation capabilities, and grow into the centerpiece of a winning organization, if given the opportunity. "Brandon, I think everyone would agree he's an enormous talent," Hornets executive vice president of basketball operations Jeff Peterson told reporters this summer . "He showed a tremendous amount of growth last season battling through an injury, but was able to continue to persevere and again help us achieve some results that made our fan base and us very, very excited, proud. [...] Of course, everyone knows he's skilled and athletic, and he has a true desire to win and continue to get better. So could not be more excited to be going into next season with Brandon Miller on our squad." To make the sort of impact that Peterson and the rest of Charlotte's braintrust believe he can, Miller will need to stay on the floor. He had surgery on that troublesome left shoulder after the season and spent the summer rehabilitating it, aiming to enter the 2026-27 campaign stronger, more stable and better able to take on the additional on- and off-court responsibilities awaiting him in Ball's absence, as one of the leaders on a team with its sights set on ending the NBA's longest ongoing postseason drought . "Do I know if we are going to be good or great?" Miller said back in August . "I know we are going to be a hard-working team. It's not about who makes the most shots. It's about who can play consistently at 110% every night. I think that's one thing we are going to take pride in."

stories.title: Lakers waive Dalton Knecht ahead of season opener, roster deadline after failing to find trade partner
stories.summary: The Lakers selected Dalton Knecht with a first-round draft pick in 2024.
stories.detailText: Dalton Knecht’s run with the Los Angeles Lakers is over. The Lakers waived Knecht on Monday, just two days before they officially open the 2026-27 NBA season, the team announced. The decision came just before the league’s deadline for teams to finalize their opening-day regular season rosters. As a result, both Bronny James and Jaden Hardy made the Lakers’ opening-day roster. James, Hardy and Knecht were widely considered the best options for the Lakers to cut to get to the 15-player maximum after they entered training camp with one too many players. The Lakers selected Knecht with the No. 17 overall pick in 2024 out of Tennessee. He was a solid bench player for the franchise as a rookie, too, averaging 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds in about 19 minutes per game off the bench. The Lakers actually cut a deal to trade him to the Charlotte Hornets ahead of the deadline in 2025, too. But that trade, which was done so the Lakers could acquire center Mark Williams, fell through after Williams failed his physical. So Knecht went back to Los Angeles, and has been there ever since. Knecht’s numbers fell harshly last season. He ended up averaging just 4.2 points in about 10 minutes per game off the bench. The Lakers were reportedly looking to trade Knecht away ahead of Monday’s roster deadline, too, ready to move on from their former first-round selection altogether. The Athletic’s Dan Woike reported that the team had engaged in multiple trade calls throughout camp, but there was “no significant trade market” for Knecht. So, as they still had one too many players on the roster, the Lakers simply opted to cut their losses on Monday and move on. Knecht had two years left on his initial four-year, $18.4 million rookie deal. “The team changed. The needs changed, the fit changed,” head coach JJ Redick said of Knecht on Friday, via The Athletic . “I think he got better as a player over the last two years. I think each guy has, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the amount of injuries we had. So, I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings, and he’s in a tough spot right now.” The Lakers will open the season on Wednesday night at home against the Golden State Warriors. It’ll mark the third season under Redick, and the first without LeBron James since 2018. James opted to leave the Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this past summer, leaving Luka Dončić as the sole star for the franchise to build around. Knecht, meanwhile, will start the season as a free agent. The 25-year-old was a thrilling player to watch in college, and he got Tennessee to the Elite Eight during his one season with the Volunteers after transferring in. But so far, his NBA career has struggled to take off. Now he’ll get the chance at a fresh start, ideally with a team that wants to keep him around.

stories.title: Warriors expect Steph Curry (ankle) to play in opener vs. Lakers
stories.summary: The Warriors expect Stephen Curry to be available for Wednesday night's season opener against the Lakers despite tweaking his right ankle during an open scrimmage Sunday.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors expect Stephen Curry to be available for Wednesday night's season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers despite tweaking his right ankle during an open scrimmage Sunday afternoon. Curry was a full participant in practice Monday morning, and Warriors coach Steve Kerr said Curry reassured him he was "fine" soon after leaving the floor in clear discomfort. Curry rolled his ankle on a dribble move from the right wing midway through the scrimmage. After the misstep, he stopped action, banged the basketball on the floor and limped to the locker room in front of a concerned arena of teammates and fans. He didn't return to the scrimmage. But Curry's ankle responded well overnight, and the medical staff cleared him to continue his ramp-up to the regular season, expecting him to play against the Lakers on Wednesday after another practice Tuesday. Curry will turn 39 in March. He spent the summer reconfiguring his routine to better manage a persistent right knee problem that forced him to miss 27 games last season. The Warriors were careful with his preseason minutes, and Kerr said they will have him practice less to ease his workload. The Warriors are already without starting wings Moses Moody and Jimmy Butler III , both rehabbing serious knee injuries and expected back midseason. Starting center Kristaps Porzingis remains out indefinitely with a private health issue and won't travel to Los Angeles with the team. Starting guard Brandin Podziemski missed Monday's practice with lower back tightness and is questionable for the opener.

stories.title: Sixers' VJ Edgecombe on playing with LeBron James: 'He's exactly old enough to be my dad, which is crazy'
stories.summary: James finished his second NBA season before Edgecombe was born in 2005.
stories.detailText: At 41 years old, LeBron James is the oldest player in the NBA as he begins his 24th season, his first with the Philadelphia 76ers. While the league constantly replenishes with players who only played one year of college basketball, James is now facing players half his age — or maybe even less than half his age. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season For instance, Cooper Flagg — last season's NBA Rookie of the Year — is 19 years old and will turn 20 in December. AJ Dybantsa, this year's No. 1 overall pick in the NBA Draft , is just a bit younger, turning 20 next January. Another of the league's youngest players is now a teammate. VJ Edgecombe turned 21 in July and is going into his second NBA season. He was the Sixers' 2025 first-round pick (No. 3 overall) after playing one season at Baylor. Speaking to ESPN's Malika Andrews, Edgecombe acknowledged he didn't think he'd ever play in a game with James, let alone be on the same team with him. Jaylen Brown on being teammates with Lebron: "The 12 year old in me is like over the moon...no glaze but you playing with one of the greatest" VJ Edgecombe: "He's exactly old enough to be my dad, which is crazy. I ain't gonna lie. His son is older than me which is crazy" pic.twitter.com/N4hMPQWwJS — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 19, 2026 "I ain't gonna lie, I thought he was going to retire like a few years ago," Edgecombe said. "So I'm like, 'Man, I'll never catch LeBron James in the NBA."' "He's exactly old enough to be my dad, which is crazy," he added. "His son is older than me, which is crazy." Edgecombe is right on that. Bronny James just turned 22 years old on Oct. 6 and is going into his third NBA season. Even a more veteran teammate like Jaylen Brown was a child when James began his NBA career in 2003. Brown remembers growing up as a basketball fan watching and admiring the four-time MVP. "The 12-year-old in me is, like, over the moon," he said. "No glaze, but you're playing with one of the greatest." The 76ers tip off the 2026-27 NBA season on Tuesday at Madison Square Garden against the defending champion New York Knicks.

stories.title: Knicks Notes: Mike Brown and Jalen Brunson on turning the page, returning New York's core players
stories.summary: After practice Monday, Knicks coach Mike Brown, as well as guards Jalen Brunson and Landry Shamet, spoke about what it means to turn the page on their championship berth and enter a new campaign with largely the same group.
stories.detailText: After practice Monday, Knicks coach Mike Brown , as well as guards Jalen Brunson and Landry Shamet , spoke about what it means to turn the page on their championship berth and enter a new campaign with largely the same group. Turning the page on a title The Knicks will kick off their 2026-27 campaign with one last celebration of their historic NBA title: a ring presentation and banner raising ceremony hosted at MSG ahead of their season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers Tuesday night. As fun as it's been to revel in their success the last few months, much of the team is already trying to move forward. "Every year, it's a new year to attack something," Brunson said. "When people say we're defending the title — I mean, that's one way to look at it, but it's something we won. We've put in our past, and now we're just trying to attack another." Shamet added that although fans across New York City are still riding the high of the championship, once the new season starts, everyone will be more focused what lies ahead. "I think the fascinating part about sports is that starting tomorrow, no one cares [about the championship]," Shamet added. "After the ceremony's over, it's 0-0. We're a competitive bunch, and by no means is anybody expecting to just coast or anything like that. That's definitely not the tone of our group." Between the ring presentation, the roar of the home crowd, and the excitement of a new season, having a ceremony immediately before the opener against Philly could be distracting. But Brown said he trusts his players to compartmentalize. "It's hard, because they're human, and there's a part of you that wants to keep celebrating, but we've got to turn it off," he said. "The challenge is to try to get them enjoy the moment, but not fully. You have to try to supress all that early, before the ceremony, so that you can quickly get not just your body, but your mind and your emotions into the task in front of you." The hard part, Shamet said, is to not get so wrapped up in what they've already accomplished that they become cocky or complacent. "I think that's maybe some of the challenge that I've read about and seen in the past that championship teams have," Shamet added. "How do you take the high in the celebration at the beginning of the game, and still go out and perform, play the brand of basketball that you'd want to play?" Jalen Brunson on Knicks fans seeing a new banner raised tomorrow night: "They deserve it. This is something that's been brewing for a long time...to share this moment with them is definitely going to be special." https://t.co/IlRiUGpGil — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 19, 2026 Shamet grateful for another year in New York For the first time in his eight-year career, Shamet is spending a third-straight season with the same team. After splitting his freshman season between the 76ers and the Clippers, he floated from the Nets, to the Suns, to the Wizards, until finally landing in the Knicks organization in 2024. He then dislocated his shoulder, got waived by the Knicks, spent a few months recovering, and worked his way from New York's' G-League affiliate back onto the major league bench. Shamet ended up a crucial piece of the Knicks bench late in the playoffs, shooting 55.6 percent and 41.7 percent from the field in Games 1 and 2 of the Finals, respectively. In June, he inked a four-year deal with the team worth $24 million, marking Shamet's first long-term commitment with a team. "It's not lost on me. I feel like I try and do a good job of not taking much for granted," Shamet said of his tenure with the Knicks. "[I've] never spent three consecutive training camps with the same organization, so feels really good ... to be here and have a familiar group and feel comfortable and confident with the people I'm around. I feel like they feel the same way about me, so I don't take that for granted at all." He's one of several key players the Knicks were able to retain in the offseason — a fact that should give them a boost against many of their Eastern Conference rivals, whose rosters saw major shakeups over the summer: Boston got Paul George and former Knick Mitchell Robinson , Philadelphia added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , Toronto welcomed Kawhi Leonard back after seven years away from the team, and Miami acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo after a lengthy trade battle with Boston. While those teams spend the early months of the season working out the kinks that come with a roster rebrand, the Knicks are hoping to lean on their well-established system to get ahead early. "[It's] very valuable," Brunson said of returning so many key players. "For us to come back, it's good to have our chemistry continue to grow, understanding that we've done it, but are we still hungry, are we still satisfied? Do we continue to get better every single day, or are we just content? That's our big question that's going to be answered within the first couple weeks of the season. However we answer it, we're going to attack it and get better every single day after that."

stories.title: Goldin Is Bringing Lakers History Closer to the Game
stories.summary: With direct access to Lakers memorabilia, the franchise's global fan base and eBay's live-commerce infrastructure, Goldin is drawing on decades of auction expertise to bring sports history to mainstream fans and established collectors alike.
stories.detailText: With direct access to Lakers memorabilia, the franchise’s global fan base and eBay’s live-commerce infrastructure, Goldin is drawing on decades of auction expertise to bring sports history to mainstream fans and established collectors alike. Magic Johnson signed his name three times across a purple Los Angeles Lakers jersey before Ken Goldin brought it to auction. The five-time NBA champion was among the Lakers legends participating in an invitation-only gathering at a private residence in West Hollywood on October 13. Public figures, private collectors, athletes, and industry figures, including Rob Veres of Burbank Sports Cards and members of the Trove Media team, gathered for an evening of live signings, historical memorabilia and auctions streamed through eBay Live. View this post on Instagram A post shared by SOMOS Index I Sports Culture & Memorabilia (@somos.index) Johnson’s signed jersey was auctioned, with proceeds benefiting the Magic Johnson Foundation. Lakers legends Kurt Rambis and Derek Fisher also participated in the evening, while Goldin presented an assortment of collectibles spanning generations of Lakers history. Elsewhere in the residence, a Wilt Chamberlain jersey photo-matched to Game 3 of the 1972 NBA Finals stood alongside a Magic Johnson jersey worn during his 1989–90 MVP season. Kobe Bryant ’s twice-signed Nike Air Zoom Huarache 2K4 sneakers, worn during his 42-point playoff performance against the San Antonio Spurs in 2004, were also on display. Five championship rings belonging to longtime Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter represented the franchise’s championship runs from 2000 to 2002 and 2009 to 2010. The evening marked the first major activation of Goldin’s multiyear partnership with the Lakers, announced in July, which named the eBay-owned company the franchise’s official auction house sponsor. Beginning October 28, Goldin will introduce weekly Wednesday auctions on eBay Live, bringing together historical memorabilia and equipment used during the current NBA season. For Ken Goldin, the choice of partner was deliberate. “Look, for me, I wanted to start at the top,” Goldin told Sam Goodman, Mantel contributor and founder of SOMOS Index, pointing to the Lakers’ championship history, international recognition and generations of culturally significant players. The agreement represents more than an opportunity to sell memorabilia associated with one of basketball’s most recognizable franchises. It connects Goldin directly with the organization producing and preserving those objects, while opening access to the global audience that gives them cultural and commercial significance. The Goldin Advantage Auction houses have traditionally relied on private collectors, dealers and consignors to bring valuable memorabilia to market. A historically significant jersey might remain in a personal collection for decades before its owner decides to sell. Goldin’s Lakers partnership introduces a different approach, establishing a direct relationship with the franchise rather than depending exclusively on owners bringing memorabilia to auction. “How does working with professional sports organizations change your approach to sourcing inventory?” Goodman asked. “For us, it gives us a guaranteed supply without competition,” Goldin responded. The agreement gives Goldin access to selected memorabilia from the Lakers’ historical archives alongside contemporary game-used equipment, including jerseys, basketballs and nets. Rather than competing for those objects once they enter private collections, the auction house can source them through the organization itself. That relationship is particularly important in a market where an object’s value depends not only on who used it, but also on the ability to establish its history. “To us, provenance and authenticity is the number one thing,” Goldin explained. “Is it real? Is it authentic? We are getting it from the source.” Acquiring memorabilia directly from the franchise provides a clearer chain of custody, connecting an item’s documented use to its eventual sale. For collectors, that provenance can be as important as the athlete or performance associated with it. Direct sourcing also changes how quickly memorabilia can reach the market. Goldin described how equipment associated with a significant performance could potentially reach auction as soon as the following day, rather than spending years circulating through private collections. The same relationship could allow collectors to pursue objects before their significance has even been established. He outlined plans for a service allowing fans to arrange the purchase of game-worn memorabilia before an upcoming matchup. A collector, for example, could request an Austin Reaves jersey without knowing whether the player will deliver an ordinary performance or a career-defining night. The distinction is significant. Historically, collectors have often pursued memorabilia after an athlete or moment has become important. Goldin’s approach could allow them to acquire objects tied to moments whose place in sports history has yet to be determined. For an auction house built around bringing desirable collectibles to market, the Lakers relationship provides a closer connection to the athletes, games and organizations responsible for creating them. The Power of the Purple and Gold The Lakers offer Goldin something beyond a collection of historic jerseys and game-used equipment. Few professional sports franchises have a cultural identity as recognizable as the Lakers. From Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant to LeBron James and Luka Dončić, the team’s history extends across generations of basketball, entertainment and popular culture. That recognition also gives Goldin access to an audience far larger than the established sports memorabilia market. “Part of our deal is that this is going to be promoted to the millions of fans that are in the Lakers database and maybe not in my auction database,” Goldin explained. For an auction house accustomed to reaching customers through collectors, dealers and existing marketplace participants, the franchise relationship creates another path to potential buyers. A lifelong Lakers fan may have attended games, purchased jerseys and followed the team’s biggest moments without ever participating in a memorabilia auction. Through the partnership, that same fan could encounter an opportunity to own an object directly connected to a favorite player or memorable performance. Goldin has previously used entertainment to introduce collecting to audiences outside the traditional hobby. Why Season 3 of Netflix’s King of Collectibles: The Goldin Touch, is Ken Goldin’s Biggest Statement Yet Netflix’s King of Collectibles: The Goldin Touch , which premiered in 2023, brought viewers inside the auction house, following the personalities, historic objects and competitive transactions that define its business. The Lakers partnership approaches audience development from another direction. Where Netflix introduced collecting through entertainment, the franchise relationship allows Goldin to reach potential customers through their existing attachment to a team and its players. Rather than asking viewers to become interested in collectibles generally, Goldin can introduce memorabilia connected to athletes and moments they already care about. The inventory itself is intended to serve a broader range of buyers. View this post on Instagram A post shared by gigi michelle (@gigimichellee) “We’re going to have something for everybody and we’re going to have something from every player,” Goldin said. Alongside premium game-worn jerseys and historically significant artifacts, Goldin plans to offer more accessible collectibles and unusual objects connected to players throughout the roster. Potential offerings include media-day jerseys, game-used basketballs, locker-room nameplates and equipment associated with the franchise. For established collectors, that creates another source of rare and historically significant memorabilia. For Lakers fans unfamiliar with auctions, it introduces collecting through a relationship they already have with the team. Exposure to the Lakers’ global audience does not guarantee that those fans will become collectors. But it gives Goldin a direct channel to potential customers beyond the people who already participate in its auctions, expanding the audience for the memorabilia the partnership brings to market. Beyond the Auction Block Ken Goldin’s experience with live selling dates back decades. Long before the rise of livestream shopping, he sold sports memorabilia to television audiences through QVC and the Home Shopping Network. In 2024, eBay acquired Goldin, connecting its established auction business with a global marketplace and digital commerce infrastructure. The Lakers partnership brings those capabilities together with something traditional auction houses cannot always count on: a continuing source of memorabilia tied to a franchise whose history is still being written. Beginning October 28, Goldin will introduce weekly Wednesday Lakers auctions through Goldin on eBay Live, offering historical collectibles alongside contemporary game-used equipment throughout the NBA season. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Goldin (@goldinco) “We’re doing so much more than an auction; we’re creating a real show each week that is entertaining, fast-paced, and interactive,” Goldin said in the company’s October announcement. For an auction business historically organized around consignments and scheduled sales, recurring programming introduces a different rhythm. Rather than waiting for individual collections to become available, Goldin can organize regular auctions around memorabilia sourced through the franchise. The NBA season provides a natural calendar, with each game creating the possibility of another significant performance, while the Lakers’ archives offer decades of material beyond the current roster. The October 13 activation offered an early example of how those elements could work together. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ROMY MARIE 🫶🏼 (@romyybae) Magic Johnson’s live jersey signing placed one of basketball’s most recognizable figures directly into the presentation of an object associated with his career. Ken Goldin brought the jersey to auction, while eBay Live extended participation beyond the collectors and guests gathered in West Hollywood. The athlete, the memorabilia and the transaction became part of the same event. Goldin’s traditional auction platform will continue offering Lakers memorabilia alongside its eBay Live programming, allowing the partnership to serve established collectors while developing a recurring format for new audiences. For Ken Goldin, whose career has spanned televised selling, high-end auctions and digital marketplaces, live commerce represents another way to connect collectors with the objects and stories that have long defined his business. The difference now is that Goldin has a direct relationship with the franchise supplying those stories. A League of Opportunities The Lakers are not the only professional sports organization Goldin is pursuing. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Goldin (@goldinco) The company has also announced a partnership with the Detroit Pistons, reflecting a broader effort to establish direct relationships with teams rather than relying solely on traditional consignment channels. During his conversation with Mantel, Goldin discussed the possibility of expanding the model across major professional sports leagues. But he made clear that the company is not interested in accumulating partnerships simply for the sake of increasing their number. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Goldin (@goldinco) “We’re not looking to sign 100 teams,” he said. Instead, Goldin described a selective approach focused on franchises with established histories, strong fan communities, recognizable identities and championship potential. The Lakers provide a particularly compelling starting point. Their decades of championships, internationally recognized players and extensive historical archives offer valuable inventory, while the team’s global audience creates opportunities to reach collectors and fans well beyond the existing auction market. Whether other franchise relationships can deliver similar results remains an open question. For Goldin, the success of the Lakers partnership will depend on more than the number of objects brought to auction. “I think success is going to not only be determined by sales,” he explained. “Success is going to be determined by selling prices. Are we getting good prices?” The company is also looking at whether the partnership attracts new bidders, increases Goldin’s visibility and generates interest from other professional sports organizations. “How much do we raise our profile? Did we gain X number of tens of thousands new bidders?” Those measures offer a clearer picture of the company’s ambitions. Strong auction results would demonstrate demand for the memorabilia itself. New bidders would suggest that access to the Lakers’ fan base is translating into customers. Additional franchise relationships could indicate that the model has applications beyond one of basketball’s most recognizable teams. None of those outcomes is guaranteed. But the partnership gives Goldin an opportunity to test how direct access to professional sports organizations can change both the supply of memorabilia and the audience participating in its sale. Goldin has spent decades building a business around bringing pieces of sports history to auction. Its partnership with the Lakers creates an opportunity to connect that business more directly with history as it unfolds.

He continued playing with the Valley Suns, however, and following the conversion of Jamaree Bouyea’s two-way contract to a standard NBA deal in March, Huntley was brought back on another two-way contract. Hamstring issues prevented Huntley from participating in the Summer League, but he put together a productive season with the Valley Suns last year. In 42 appearances, the 6’11” big man averaged 15.4 points and 7.9 rebounds in 27 minutes per game, shooting 63% from the field, 34% from beyond the arc, and 67% from the free throw line. Despite that production, Phoenix has decided to move on from Huntley as it continues adjusting its roster ahead of the regular season. His departure, along with Brea’s, leaves the Suns with one open two-way contract spot and one standard roster spot.

(Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ladies and gentlemen, Adam Silver has done it again. The commissioner and the rest of his coroporate teammates at the NBA office continue to ensure the league’s viewers have the maximum amount of fun, thanks to the endless amount of jerseys each franchise wears. That, of course, includes your Boston Celtics. Boston is one of eight franchises to have a “Specter” edition uniform bestowed upon them this season. *NSFW Image Below pic.twitter.com/cNMcHpHv7y — GreenRunsDeep (@CelticsGRD) October 19, 2026 When I saw this, I almost spiked my phone. What a disgusting piece of moneygrabbing slop. Now, I’m the defininition of a traditionalist, so there’s definitely some bias here. I think the home team should always wear white, and road teams can wear any of their more colorful uniforms. With that being said, there’s simply no way that these should’ve seen the light of day. The Northern Lights-esque design doesn’t work. The small font that reads “Boston” (you might not even have noticed it on the chest of the jersey) looks ridiculous. Who is this even for? There are seven other fanbases who are likely asking themselves the same question. The New York Knicks, Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks, Los Angeles Lakers, Sacramento Kings, Philadelphia 76ers, and Golden State Warriors will all feature a similar looking monstrosity in their respective wardrobes this season. Ironically, the league picked its eight oldest franchises to force these disguting unis on as part of this Specter series. “The new Specter Edition uniforms open a new chapter in how team identity for the Sacramento Kings, Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks, Golden State Warriors, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Los Angeles Lakers and Boston Celtics — the teams tracing their history back to the earliest chapters of the NBA — appears on court,” the league wrote in an official release last month . “Bringing forward the same obsession with the game that defines the NBA Standard Issue collection, each uniform features details inspired by the franchises’ history, city heritage and fan culture.“ You know what would’ve been a great way to honor history? Maybe whip up some cool throwback jerseys. It’s possible. We’ve seen the Celtics run with throwbacks in the past, despite not having changed much about their uniforms over the course of 80 years. Having read through the full press release, it seems like the NBA is trying to capitalize on the hypebeast culture of wearing silly looking things just because they’re rare. Featured several times throughout is the “1:1” tag. More or less, the goal of the entire charade is to break into the fashion world by having players serve as models for this new line. Does the league know that they can just release obscure merch without making the teams wear it? There is some “good” news woven into this story, though. The Celtics will only put these things on three times this season. Three, by the way, is the bare minimum amount of games that teams are required to wear any special edition uniform. stories.title: Mavericks waive center Dwight Powell after 12-year run
stories.summary: The Mavericks waived longtime center Dwight Powell on Monday, likely ending his 12-year run with the franchise.
stories.detailText: DALLAS -- The Dallas Mavericks waived longtime center Dwight Powell on Monday, likely ending his 12-year run with the franchise after he was the secondary piece in a trade that brought Rajon Rondo from Boston. Powell was a late add just as training camp started last month, raising the possibility of a 13th season with the Mavericks. Dallas already had the full allotment of 15 guaranteed contracts, so keeping Powell would have forced the team to release one of those players. The 35-year-old Powell was in and out of the rotation throughout his time with the Mavericks. He has played all but five of his 768 games with Dallas, including 266 starts. He has averaged 6.5 points, 4.2 rebounds and 17.5 minutes per game. Powell joined the Mavericks in December 2014 when he and Rondo were part of a deal that included five players and two draft picks. Rondo and then-coach Rick Carlisle clashed, and Rondo left without playing a full season with Dallas. Powell played the next 11 full seasons with the Mavericks. "Dwight was the consummate professional throughout his 12 seasons with the Mavericks and embodies everything you want in someone representing your organization," president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri said. "He's a tireless worker, an incredible teammate and someone whose impact extends well beyond the basketball court and into the Dallas community."

stories.title: Why Celtics vs. Pistons is opening NBA season in rare daytime game
stories.summary: The 2026-27 NBA regular season will officially start with an afternoon game on NBC between the Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons. Here's why.
stories.detailText: The first game of the 2026-27 NBA regular season will officially tip off in the middle of the afternoon, and NBC hopes it can become an annual addition to the league's traditional opening night schedule. The Detroit Pistons are set to host the Boston Celtics at 3 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Oct. 20, with "College Gameday-style activations," a "Blue Carpet" experience, a marching band rendition of "Roundball Rock" and other special festivities planned around Little Caesars Arena and downtown Detroit throughout the day, according to NBA league officials. The afternoon tip is an experiment conceived by the NBA and NBC entering Year 2 of their massive 11-year, $27-billion media rights partnership , with the goal of turning opening night into an all-day event. "We kind of challenged the NBA," NBC Sports Executive Vice President Justin Byczek told USA TODAY Sports . "We think opening day should be expanded, and we'd love to be the network that gets behind it, and over the course of the next decade, let's try to understand where opening day can get to." Why the NBA is playing an afternoon game on opening day This will be the first time in 15 years that more than two games will be played on the first day of the NBA season, and it only happened in 2011 because of a lockout-shortened schedule. It will also be the first-ever NBA opening-day tripleheader broadcast nationally. NBC's opening night coverage for the 2026-27 season features the ring ceremony and banner raising for the defending NBA champion New York Knicks, their first game against LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers and a Western Conference Finals rematch between the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. But the network saw an opportunity to generate excitement before the two primetime windows that have typically defined the NBA's regular season debut. NBC pointed to strong viewership for its 2026 Major League Baseball Opening Day doubleheader, which also began with an afternoon game. NBC is confident putting Celtics vs. Pistons on a national broadcast network in the afternoon can add to the buzz leading into the Knicks' pregame title coronation, with coverage from Madison Square Garden on streaming platform Peacock bridging the gap between the first two games of the tripleheader. "The benefit of a decade-long partnership is the ability to test and to try new things," said Byczek, who oversees programming and rights management for NBC Sports. "We pushed them pretty hard to kind of say we really believe this is going to be a good opportunity to add some excitement to opening day. They went out as a great partner and found the right combination of people and teams and partners and arenas and folks that wanted to raise their arm and get behind it." NBA senior vice president for broadcast content Paul Benedict said it wasn't a hard sell. The league wanted to lean more into opening night's spot as a distinctive event on the sports calendar. The NBA, through NBC's wide reach as a national broadcast network, sees a chance to create excitement throughout the day on platforms more likely to attract the casual fans that can grow the product moving forward. For NBC, this is another way to potentially enhance the value of its NBA package and create the tentpole events that attract more viewers. The NBA gets an additional standalone national showcase game on a day and time in which it will face minimal competition from other major professional sports. "The conversations with NBC have always been built around not even just a tripleheader, but the entirety of the day," Benedict told USA TODAY Sports. "The thinking being when you turn on 'The Today Show,' you're going to get some NBA flavor. That's pretty exciting for us, the opportunity to be on NBC and celebrate the start of the season." How NBA and NBC picked Celtics vs Pistons for opening day game Finding the right host was also crucial. Not every NBA fanbase and city wants a day game to start the season. It's not part of the sport's culture like MLB opening day or the first Sunday afternoon of NFL season. Byczek compared the process to a "Jenga puzzle" in terms of figuring out what franchises were interested in hosting the game, and then identifying an opponent that would present the best possible matchup for a national audience. The NBA brought the idea of hosting an afternoon opener to "some teams," according to Benedict. "Detroit raised their hand and was all-in from Day One," he said, "and to put a 60-win team on that's built such a great sports community, specifically around the downtown area where they can rally around it, was appealing. And then when you pair them with the Boston Celtics , that just fit the criteria of adding another elite matchup if you're going to turn this into a tripleheader. The Pistons have really bought into this." Neither the league nor NBC committed to an afternoon game to start the NBA season beyond this year, with both sides emphasizing the results from Tuesday will dictate what happens next. "We'll evaluate it and see whether this is something that is here to stay. Who knows? Maybe we expand it from here as well," Byczek said. "We don't ever want to remain status quo. We want to test new things, try new things, and this one ... hit us right between the eyes of let's try to do more on opening day." What time is Celtics vs Pistons on NBA opening day? The NBA opening day game between the Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20, is set to tip off at 3 p.m. ET. How to watch Celtics vs Pistons: TV channel, live streaming Date : Tuesday, Oct. 20 Time : 3 p.m. ET Location : Little Caesars Arena (Detroit) TV : NBC Streaming : Peacock, Fubo This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why Celtics vs. Pistons is opening NBA season in rare daytime game

stories.title: Phoenix moves on from Koby Brea ahead of the regular season
stories.summary: After struggling from three-point range in Summer League and the preseason, Brea loses his spot as Phoenix opens a two-way slot.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 28: Koby Brea #14 of the Phoenix Suns poses for a portrait during NBA media day on September 28, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Phoenix Suns continue to fine-tune every aspect of their roster in preparation for the 2026–27 season. They’ve brought in Duop Reath on a two-way contract, waived Haywood Highsmith , extended Oso Ighodaro , and picked up the option on Ryan Dunn. And now? They’ve waived second-year sharpshooter Koby Brea, per HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto. Fuego no more, per @mikeascotto pic.twitter.com/VA6a02scSX — Suns JAM Session Podcast (@SunsJAM) October 19, 2026 Brea was selected 41st overall in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Kentucky, following an illustrious collegiate career in which he established himself as one of the best three-point shooters in the NCAA. Unfortunately, that shooting ability hasn’t consistently translated to the NBA level. He appeared in 12 games for Phoenix last season, connecting on 13-of-30 attempts from beyond the arc, good for 43.3%. The hope was that he’d build upon that production through Summer League and the preseason, continuing his development as a reliable perimeter threat. But during Summer League, Brea shot 8-of-28 from deep, good for 28.6%. That was followed by a preseason in which he connected on 3-of-10 attempts, shooting 30% from beyond the arc. When your primary translatable skill is shooting, and you’re struggling to consistently knock down shots, you become vulnerable. You become expendable. And for an organization that values flexibility throughout its roster, that’s a difficult position to find yourself in. Unfortunately for Koby Brea, the Suns have opted to move on, leaving one two-way contract spot available as the team continues making its final roster adjustments ahead of the regular season. The bigger picture here is roster flexibility. Brea showed that he could knock down shots in limited NBA opportunities, but his struggles in Summer League and the preseason put his greatest strength into question. With the regular season approaching, the Suns have decided to open that two-way spot rather than wait for his shooting to come around. It’s a tough business, particularly for a young player. But in Phoenix, every roster spot needs to serve a purpose.

stories.title: Tacko Fall is a unique player with a unique opportunity
stories.summary: Tacko Fall would be the third player 7-foot-6 or taller to suit up for the Sixers.
stories.detailText: CAMDEN, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 28: Tacko Fall #99 of the Philadelphia 76ers poses for a portrait during media day at the Philadelphia 76ers Training Complex on September 28, 2026 in Camden, New Jersey. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you had a nickel for every player 7-foot-6 or taller to suit up for the Sixers, you’d have two nickels. But it’s still crazy it’s happened twice. The 7-foot-7 Manute Bol and the 7-foot-6 Shawn Bradley both played in parts of three seasons for the Sixers. Tacko Fall is hoping the third time is the charm. The 7-foot-6 Senegalese big man is back in the NBA after signing a two-way contract this past weekend. When/if he does take the court for the Sixers, it will be his first NBA minutes since December of 2021. While there’s been intrigue about Fall and his unique size dating back to his days at UCF, it also came with questions about his mobility and ability to deal with elite athletes. Those were doubts Fall let creep into his own mind at times. His years overseas have put him in a better place. “Physically and mentally,” Fall said about where he’s improved. “I feel like when you — I won’t even say seven-foot-plus — but when you reach a certain height, there’s a picture that most people have of you of, ‘OK, can he do this? Can he do that?’ Where mentally you might doubt [yourself], but for me, I feel like I was always capable of that, it’s just pushing myself to realize that and be consistent with it, and that also comes with being in great physical condition.” Luckily for him, there are a couple familiar faces around to help him as he reacclimates to the NBA. Fall and Sixers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey overlapped in Cleveland in 2021-22. By that time, Gansey was transitioning from assistant general manager to general manager under Koby Altman. Fall was in his third season after two years with the Boston Celtics. Fall doesn’t take that familiarity for granted. “Great guy. Always positive,” Fall said of Gansey after practice Sunday. “We joke around. Like he would walk around the court every morning [in Cleveland]. I would see him walk around, and he’s doing the same thing [here], and he’s been like that for years. But I’m happy also. Like I got to come here and see another familiar face, which kind of helps with the comfort level.” On the court is an even bigger connection. Newcomer Jaylen Brown was teammates with Fall for both of his seasons with the Celtics. The two became extremely close, with Fall naming Brown the godfather of his second daughter. Even as Fall’s career took him far, far away from Boston, the two remained close. Imagine telling either of them that they’d reunite in Philadelphia. “Jaylen is my brother,” Fall said. “We built a great relationship throughout the years, even while I was away. He’s family. … Throughout the years, we built such a great relationship, and for me, I’m very happy that we get to play together.” But this isn’t just a feel-good story. The Sixers need depth at the backup center position. Fall offers a unique option in several ways. Once Ariel Hukporti went down with a season-ending Achilles injury, the Sixers had little recourse to make a move. They have 14 of 15 standard roster spots filled, but are hard-capped at the first apron, meaning they’re unable to sign a veteran center to a minimum deal. Their simplest path was adding a two-way player. In Fall, they get a player with professional basketball experience, both in the NBA and overseas. The 30-year-old has been on a journey since going undrafted out of UCF in 2019. After two seasons in Boston and one in Cleveland, Fall has spent the bulk of his time in China, with a stint in Australia mixed in. The most obvious strength for Fall is his size. At 7-foot-6 and 311 pounds, he will be the tallest active player in the NBA once he takes the court. It makes it obvious where Fall could fit in the Sixers’ center mix. With Joel Embiid’s health always a concern, those playing behind him are critical to team success. Fall said going up against Embiid in practice has been “very motivating,” and called the former MVP “probably the best big in the NBA.” That’s what makes it critical to have depth behind Embiid. With Adem Bona and Jabari Walker (and the currently banged-up Dean Wade and Dominick Barlow) being a little undersized, Fall is an ideal option for when the Sixers come across a bigger opponent — especially if it happens during a back-to-back. Though he missed all of the preseason and most of camp, the team was intrigued by what they saw prior to his hip injury. “I did get to see a good chunk of him prior to kind of the injury,” Nick Nurse said. “How I plan on using him, probably remains to be seen. But kind of was intrigued and liked what I saw in the fall. So we’ll see what happens.” Fall spoke candidly about the scrutiny he’s faced because of his size and perceived lack of mobility. He bided his time overseas, building confidence in himself as a player and person. Now, he’s just looking for an opportunity. “I was a little speechless, to be honest,” Fall said about learning he’d been offered a two-way deal. “Like I said, I’ve had quite a few challenges since I left, and … after all these years and after all the hard work, I think it means a lot more.”

But according to his head coach, JJ Redick, the 25-year-old is ready for the challenges and incubated by plenty of people and resources to make the experience as easy as possible for him. “I think he wants to embrace that. I think that’s why he wanted to be a Laker and why he wanted to be here was because of the fact that there are stakes every single night when you wear a Lakers uniform,” Redick told reporters postgame on Friday. “We’ve had a number of conversations. They all have a chip on their shoulder about it and they want to make Lakers fans proud and I know they will.” Kessler clearly recognizes the positive environment being fostered and sounds as though he’s taking a healthy approach to all of it, excited for the chance he’s afforded to play for such a renowned organization. “The support system around me, with my teammates, the coaching staff, front office, I mean, they’re fantastic,” Kessler said following Los Angeles’ preseason finale . “They’re very vocal about, obviously being a Lakers big, there’s a certain legacy with that, but not to look at it as pressure, more so as an opportunity. So that’s kind of the attitude I’m going in with it.” After appearing in the Lakers’ final two preseason outings , Kessler will make his regular-season debut Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors, where he’ll take his first genuine crack at proving himself on the court to the Lakers and their fanbase. stories.summary: Dalton Knecht’s time in Los Angeles could be nearing an end
stories.detailText: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 13: Dalton Knecht #4 of the Los Angeles Lakers is guarded by Will Richard #3 of the Golden State Warriors in the fourth quarter of a preseason game at T-Mobile Arena on October 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Warriors defeated the Lakers 101-89. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, Jake Fischer reported the Los Angeles Lakers and Milwaukee Bucks “held exploratory trade discussions” around a deal that would send Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee and Jericho Sims to Los Angeles to solve Los Angeles’ roster crunch ahead of the regular season starting Tuesday. Marc Stein reinforced that notion, indicating Sims is perhaps not the Lakers’ lone target as they seek front-court help and look to trim the roster from 16 players down to 15. “The Lakers spent the weekend trying to find a workable trade to ship out Dalton Knecht and maybe even bring back a big man — such as Milwaukee’s Jericho Sims as Jake revealed in his Thursday piece — to shave their roster from 16 guaranteed contracts to 15,” Stein wrote . “If no trade can be found, they’ll have to waive Knecht (or someone else) by the cut-down buzzer.” After delighting early in his rookie season, including a 37-point outburst against the Utah Jazz, and even starting a handful of games, Knecht saw his playing time dwindle as he ultimately fell out of the 2024-25 playoff rotation. Last season, he received another crack at rotation minutes but struggled mightily and became a non-factor by year’s end, logging just 107 minutes from February onward, including the playoffs. Knecht’s primary allure out of college was his jumper but he’s been merely a good outside shooter in the NBA, converting 36.8% of his 3s through two seasons. His lack of strength and lateral mobility severely hinders his defense while he’s not a threat as a passer or off-the-dribble scorer. His rigid offensive skill-set and detrimental defense have understandably prevented him from carving out a consistent role with the Lakers. He’d have to be a truly elite shooter to mitigate his shortcomings elsewhere and that’s not been the case. Knecht was not a second-round flier or late-first gamble. He was selected 17th overall in 2024. Him not panning out is a sharp indictment of the Lakers’ front office. Knecht joined Jalen Hood-Schifino as one of Los Angeles’s two top-20 selections since 2020 and neither has established themselves as legitimate contributors during their rookie contracts. Both picks represent team-building failures and reasons the Lakers haven’t been actual title contenders over that span. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Santi Aldama’s timeframe for return remains a mystery
stories.summary: The latest from head coach Dusty May does little to firm up a return to action for Aldama
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TX - SEPTEMBER 25: Santi Aldama #34 of the Dallas Mavericks poses for a portrait during NBA media day on September 25, 2026 in Dallas, Texas at American Airlines Center. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Glenn James/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks are just a few short days away from the start of the 2026-2027 NBA season. The Mavericks wrapped their preseason slate with a somewhat dismal 1-3 record, but the silver lining is that they welcomed back Kyrie Irving (who looked very much like the player we remember) and suffered no new injuries in the process. No new injuries does not mean the Mavericks are truly at full strength, of course. Dereck Lively remains sidelined and likely will be for the foreseeable future. Joining him is newly acquired Santi Aldama. Aldama had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee back on March 17 when he was still a member of the Memphis Grizzlies. That ended his season early and resulted in an absence from which he has still not returned. He sat out all four preseason games. Strangely, there has been relatively little news regarding Aldama’s timetable for return despite the fact he figures on being a significant contributor. Now on the eve of the season, Mike Curtis reports a small update Santi Aldama (right knee surgery) remains without a timetable to return. Dusty May said he "doesn't know yet" if he'll play in Wednesday's season opener against the #Rockets . — Mike Curtis (@MikeACurtis2) October 18, 2026 Head coach Dusty May said “he doesn’t know yet” if Aldama will be available for Wednesday night’s season opener. The comment is straightforward, yet somewhat puzzling. Wednesday is mere days away at this point, so the comment seems to suggest a return is imminent, even if not for the season opener. May was earlier quoted as saying Aldama was “getting much, much closer” after a solid practice, and he is roughly seven months to the day removed from surgery. The Mavericks have played injury news very close to the vest under the new regime of Masai Ujiri, Mike Schmitz and May, so we are in somewhat uncharted territory of how to truly read this messaging. Nonetheless, and at the expense of assuming too much, it seems irresponsible for May to suggest favorable progress and a potential return as soon as this week if Aldama is in fact weeks (or more) away. Aldama is a seven-foot stretch big that should be able to add a meaningful dynamic to the Mavericks on both sides of the ball. Having him back and at full health is critical to the Mavs’ success this season, especially with Lively expected to be out for an extended period. While we can only speculate on the exact return date for Aldama, the facts seem to suggest that it will be sooner than later. I invite you to follow me @_80MPH on X, and check back often at Mavs Moneyball for all the latest on the Dallas Mavericks.

stories.title: PTH Roundtable: who will break out?
stories.summary: From the development program that brought two MIPs, who could be the third?

(Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the second of a series of roundtable questions I’m asking the staff here at Peachtree Hoops about the Hawks this upcoming season. The second question: who will have the biggest breakout performance and why? Wes: For me, Aaron Wiggins has a chance to shine in a featured bench role. The Thunder were so deep that Wiggins often ended up on the fringe of the rotation, but he has legitimate creation ability off the bounce and a good enough, though shaky, feel to be a CJ McCollum-lite bucket getter. I think he’ll be a better team defender and passer than McCollum, however, and play in the screen, move and quick decision offense that Quin Snyder has set up. He’s just 27, the same age as Nickeil Alexander-Walker’s breakout last season. Maybe, just maybe, the Hawks can make it three straight Most Improved Player award winners. Garrett: I’m going with Aaron Wiggins. The Hawks have shown what they can do when players get the right opportunity — just ask Dyson Daniels and Nickeil Alexander-Walker. I think Wiggins could be the next player to benefit from that environment. He has the tools to flourish in Quin Snyder’s system, and I like the idea of him becoming a dependable sixth man who provides a spark on both ends. Graham: A couple Hawks spring to mind. I would agree with the sentiment that Aaron Wiggins has an opportunity to really excel here with Atlanta. There should be ample opportunities for corner threes for him here, and he shot 48% in the right corner from three. If he can swing his left corner threes up from 30% this season he becomes another three-point option for Jalen Johnson, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, CJ McCollum, and Dyson Daniels to kick out to the corner to. But in the interest of something different – prior to his injury – I would have enjoyed to see how Mo Gueye’s development would have looked like this season. Gueye’s improved touch from three-point range in addition to his length and athleticism are still interesting elements to monitor this season. I don’t have anything more to really add; I was just really looking forward to seeing more Mo Gueye. Asa Newell is also someone I’m really interested to see in Year 2; he had a really encouraging touch from three and could roll to the rim, but it just became harder to play him as the Hawks began to zone in on an automatic playoff berth. Jalen Johnson was in a similar boat in his rookie season, and now I wonder if Newell may follow a similar step in Year 2 where he gets real minutes this season. If he does, I expect him to be productive.

stories.title: Report: Sixers ‘would have strong interest’ in center Moussa Cisse
stories.summary: The 6-foot-11 Cisse is a name to watch as the Sixers look to bring in another backup center option.
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 25: Moussa Cisse #30 of the Dallas Mavericks poses for portraits at Mavericks Media Day at American Airlines Center on September 25, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the GettyImages License Agreement. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret that backup center is currently the biggest question mark for the Philadelphia 76ers’ roster, a situation exacerbated by Ariel Hukporti’s season-ending Achilles injury. As Mike Gansey surveys the NBA landscape for a solution, one name that has come up is current Dallas Mavericks center Moussa Cisse. Per reporting from Marc Stein : “If Cissé were to be waived Monday and then clear waivers Wednesday, I’m also told that the 76ers and Lakers would have strong interest in signing him to a two-way deal even though neither team currently has a two-way opening.” However: “ The Stein Line has learned, however, that Cissé is a real candidate to be claimed off waived in the event he is let go. Chicago, sources say, has interest in the high-energy big man. I’m told Atlanta also has interest even though the Hawks don’t currently have an open standard spot.” Obviously, there are a few if-then’s in play here. The Mavericks would need to waive Cisse, no one would have to pick him up off waivers (something Stein thinks would happen), and he would need to select Philadelphia as his two-way spot destination (something I think would have a good chance of happening given the relatively clear path to some playing time). On Monday, it became increasingly less likely Dallas would be waiving Cisse, as they instead released veteran Dwight Powell. The Dallas Mavericks are waiving veteran center Dwight Powell, sources tell ESPN. — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 19, 2026 So I wouldn’t be ordering those Cisse custom black Iverson-era jerseys just yet. Still, the 6-foot-11, 24-year-old is highly athletic and fits the rim-running, shot blocker role the Sixers are looking for in a backup. He’s a name to keep an eye on over the next few days. More broadly looking at the center position, Philadelphia has a few options at the moment. Joel Embiid is healthy and ready to start on opening night against the New York Knicks. The team also feels good about Adem Bona returning from his foot injury to take the floor after missing the entire preseason. Bona recently had this to say to reporters about making his way back to the court the last few weeks: “Mentally, it’s been great. I’ve been able to come back. Getting back out there, working with the team. I’ve had amazing practices with the team. It’s been great. I’m feeling good and excited to get back out there on the court. It’s been going good so far.” He added the following on his availability for the opener: “Yeah. It’s going to come down to the coaches and the medical staff, but I’m just day to day and I’m excited for (Tuesday) night.” With Jabari Walker and Dean Wade (though he’s also banged up) available as small-ball five options in certain situations, the Sixers appear set as long as everyone is healthy. For games where Embiid is sitting due to load management on a back-to-back, we would expect recent two-way signing Tacko Fall to assume some minutes. The Sixers have five back-to-backs prior to Dec. 4. Dec. 4 is a significant date because given the pro-rated nature minimum signings against the salary cap, that is when the team would be able to fill the 15th roster spot with a free agent center option and still remain under the salary cap apron. Kevin Love is one name mentioned often due to the LeBron connection. Another option would be to trade for someone making around the minimum, with Justin Edwards a salary-match candidate with a $2.4 million contract this season and a team option next season that would effectively operate as an expiring. Philadelphia could certainly go the trade route with Cisse, for example. Undoubtedly, the Sixers would like to have more confident options at their disposal. However, given the strength of the rest of the roster, there are certainly worse problems a team could have heading into a season. We know the front office will continue to monitor the market and look for the best path forward in the days and weeks ahead.

stories.title: LeBron Log: Debut history, taking charge and a limited-edition SLAM cover
stories.summary: Before LeBron James begins his fifth NBA chapter Tuesday, revisit his four previous team debuts and two early moments from his time with the Sixers.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log: Debut history, taking charge and a limited-edition SLAM cover originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Are you counting down the hours yet? On Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden, LeBron James will make his regular-season debut for the Sixers and begin his record 24th NBA season. Philadelphia is his fourth franchise and fifth NBA stint, counting his two runs in Cleveland. It’s happening. This season will bring the obvious milestones and memorable performances. It will also bring smaller moments that help tell the story of James’ time in Philadelphia. The LeBron Log will keep track of both. Check back throughout the season for new entries. For now, let’s get started with No. 1. TEAM DEBUTS Tuesday’s setting carries its own twist. James told ESPN’s Dave McMenamin at Sixers media day that he had “visions” of playing at Madison Square Garden and finishing his career there. The Knicks’ championship changed those plans. Instead, James will begin his Philadelphia chapter from the visiting locker room while New York raises its championship banner. Few road arenas have treated him better. James owns a 24-9 record in 33 games at Madison Square Garden, averaging 28.2 points, 7.4 assists and 6.9 rebounds. His previous debut games with new teams and stints have not gone nearly as well. Oct. 29, 2003: Cavaliers at Kings An 18-year-old James recorded 25 points, nine assists, six rebounds and four steals in his first NBA game. He shot 12 of 20 from the floor, but Sacramento won, 106-92. Oct. 26, 2010: Heat at Celtics The highly anticipated debut of Miami’s James-Dwyane Wade-Chris Bosh trio began in Boston. James scored 31 points, but the Celtics held off the Heat, 88-80. Oct. 30, 2014: Knicks at Cavaliers This is the closest parallel to Tuesday. James’ return to Cleveland produced a deafening reception and enormous expectations. The Knicks spoiled the homecoming. James finished with 17 points, five rebounds, four assists and eight turnovers as New York won, 95-90. Oct. 18, 2018: Lakers at Trail Blazers James opened his Lakers career with 26 points, 12 rebounds and six assists. Portland still handed Los Angeles a 128-119 loss. That makes four previous stint debuts and four losses. James averaged 24.8 points, 6.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists across those games. Tuesday gives him his first opportunity to win one. The same franchise that spoiled his Cleveland return will stand in his way again. TAKING CHARGE Friday’s preseason finale offered an early example of the smaller moments worth tracking throughout James’ first season in Philadelphia. With 8:56 remaining in the third quarter and the Sixers leading the Celtics, 69-62, Luka Garza missed a three-pointer. Ron Harper Jr. grabbed the offensive rebound before the ball returned to Garza. James established position outside the restricted area and absorbed the contact from the 6-foot-10, 243-pound center. The whistle blew for a charge, and the Sixers’ bench erupted. There was more behind the celebration than one preseason possession. Maxey said the Sixers had encountered a similar situation during practice. Adem Bona rolled toward the basket with James waiting in his path, but the 41-year-old moved aside. James assured his teammates that he would take the contact once they played an actual game. “We don’t want Bona running Bron over,” Maxey joked. James kept his word, putting his body in front of a center during the Sixers’ final exhibition game. The moment also stood out to 20-year-old rookie Labaron Philon. “Everybody jumped up off the bench and was pretty happy for him that a guy really that old was still putting his body on the line for us in a preseason game,” Philon said. “That really tells it all. … I hope he can bring that to Tuesday and for the rest of the season. I want to see some more of those.” EXTRA, EXTRA, READ ALL ABOUT IT James appeared on a SLAM cover before he played a minute in the NBA. In August 2002, James and fellow high school star Sebastian Telfair shared the cover of SLAM 62. The issue was titled “The Takeover,” and its cover predicted that the two teenagers were about to rule the basketball world. View this post on Instagram More than 24 years later, James is back on the cover. The Sixers star fronts SLAM 265 in his new No. 23 uniform. The cover reads, “This is my last run. Part II,” followed by the title, “Leaving the Legacy.” The standard edition costs $13.99. It is the first of five covers for SLAM’s December 2026/January 2027 issue and includes 82 pages and a pullout poster. SLAM also opened a 48-hour ordering window for a $65 Orange Metal version. It will remain available through Wednesday at 11 a.m. ET. Each copy will be numbered, and 24 customers will randomly receive an even rarer Platinum Metal edition instead. A $125 Gold Metal version, limited to 94 copies, has already sold out. View this post on Instagram The first cover announced “The Takeover.” The latest is about “Leaving the Legacy.” Twenty-four years of James’ basketball life, captured by two covers.
