stories.title: Rams suffer several major injuries, including to WR Adams, who's out 6-10 weeks
stories.summary: Rams wideout Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and he will be sidelined for six to 10 weeks, coach Sean McVay announced.
stories.detailText: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring in Sunday's home loss to the Arizona Cardinals , and he will be sidelined for six to 10 weeks, coach Sean McVay announced Monday. It wasn't the only major injury suffered by a significant Rams player Sunday. Poona Ford will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps, and fellow defensive tackle Kobie Turner will be out four to six weeks because of a groin injury. In addition, kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL in the contest, and he will be sidelined for the remainder of the campaign. The Rams had just signed Grupe last week after releasing the struggling Harrison Mevis . The injuries are the latest hits for a Rams team that entered the season as Super Bowl favorites but sits at 2-4 after six weeks. Star defensive end Myles Garrett has played just one game for the team after he was acquired in a blockbuster offseason trade. Garrett, who is on injured reserve due to a knee injury, will not return to practice this week, McVay said.

stories.title: John Harbaugh: Giants 'honing in on' QB decision for Sunday vs. Texans
stories.summary: The Giants are "honing in on" a decision on who will start at quarterback for Sunday's game against the Texans, coach John Harbaugh said Monday.
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants were unwilling to name a starting quarterback one day after J.J. McCarthy almost completed a miraculous comeback in relief of Jameis Winston against the New Orleans Saints . Coach John Harbaugh is choosing between McCarthy and Winston for Sunday on the road against the Houston Texans . "We're working through that now," Harbaugh said Monday. "Honing in on a decision." McCarthy, who came to the Giants in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings late last month, threw for 243 yards after entering the game with just under 12 minutes remaining. It was the second-most passing yards in a fourth quarter by a quarterback who didn't start over the past 25 years. McCarthy led three scoring drives and had the Giants in the red zone before falling short in the final seconds of a 34-27 loss to the Saints. Winston was unbeaten coming into Sunday in three starts for the Giants this season. He threw for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Saints. Harbaugh is trying to figure out who gives the Giants the best chance to beat a Texans team with a fierce pass rush. Houston is third in the NFL with 18 sacks. The Giants (3-2-1) have a bye week following the matchup. "Like every personnel decision we make, what gives us the best chance to win the football game at this given time? Or what combination of players and schemes and things like that give us the best chance to, in this case, move the ball, score points, protect the football, etc.?" Harbaugh said. "So all the things that help us win." Harbaugh said after the game Sunday that how they played would be the most important factor. It was hard to argue with McCarthy's performance. The former top-10 pick for the Vikings did his part. Now it's on Harbaugh. "The only thing I'm focused on is getting better each and every day," McCarthy said after the game. "At the end of the day, Coach Harbaugh has to make a lot of decisions. Those are his decisions. I trust him wholeheartedly with any decision he makes." The Giants are taking it all into consideration though, including the opponent being Houston on Sunday and what is best for the team in the future. The bye week is a consideration as well. It could serve as a natural landing spot for McCarthy with the extra time allowing him to get comfortable with an offense he's still learning. "I think it's all part of it, sure," Harbaugh said. The Giants coach added that part of the reason for not disclosing his starter at this point of the week is to gain a competitive advantage. He believes every little thing matters. But perhaps the biggest factor in the quarterback decision is how much McCarthy's presence in the lineup can help the Giants' run game. New York has struggled badly to run the ball in recent weeks despite Harbaugh's desire for the Giants to be a running team. Their running backs had 14 carries for 34 yards Sunday. McCarthy would allow the Giants to utilize more of the offense they designed for starter Jaxson Dart leading into the season. But Dart hurt a knee in Week 2 and forced them to turn to Winston. They catered their offense to Winston's strengths as a result. That meant few zone reads and less of the quarterback on the move. It seems to have negatively affected the Giants' overall run game. McCarthy with his increased mobility and ability to run could provide a boost. "The elements that we're talking about with some of the read plays and some of the different things you do moving the quarterback around, those are definitely things that are part of the equation," Harbaugh said. The Giants have their first team meeting of the week Tuesday and practice Wednesday. The expectation is that a decision will be made before they take the field.

stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Rams have placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he injured his right knee in the team's Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals , the team announced Monday. Coach Sean McVay said that Grupe has a torn ACL. The Rams have not announced a corresponding move at kicker. Grupe was playing in his first game with Los Angeles after he was signed off the New York Jets ' practice squad last week. Grupe was signed to replace Harrison Mevis , who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills . But after making a 44-yard field goal in the opening quarter Sunday, Grupe hurt his right knee on the ensuing kickoff while trying to make a tackle. After the game, Grupe was in the locker room with a big brace on his right leg and crutches at his locker. The Rams play the Raiders in Las Vegas in Week 7.

stories.title: Patriots place WR Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on IR
stories.summary: The Patriots have placed Romeo Doubs on IR.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Just as the New England Patriots welcomed back top receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve, they've lost another top receiver, Romeo Doubs , to a shoulder injury. The club officially placed Doubs on injured reserve Monday, one day after he landed hard on his right shoulder while making a diving 42-yard touchdown catch in a 26-19 win over the New York Jets . Doubs, who left the game after the touchdown and didn't return, has 14 receptions for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season, his first in New England. He will miss at least the next four games, beginning Thursday night when the Patriots (4-2) visit the Chicago Bears (4-2) at Soldier Field. New England then visits the Miami Dolphins and hosts the Green Bay Packers before facing the Detroit Lions in Munich. Its bye week follows. Injuries have been a defining characteristic of the Patriots' 2026 campaign, beginning in the spring when they lost No. 2 tight end Julian Hill to a season-ending knee injury. Others placed on IR during the season include starting right guard Mike Onwenu (ankle) and his replacement, Greg Van Roten (hip), No. 3 offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (ankle), starting fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle/knee), receiver Mack Hollins (calf) and punter Bryce Baringer (lower body). On Sunday against the Jets, the Patriots had been looking forward to having Doubs paired with Brown, as they had played only two-plus quarters together before Brown sustained a high right ankle sprain in the season opener. Brown was activated from IR on Saturday. The Patriots invested heavily in both players this offseason to give quarterback Drake Maye a new top of the receiver depth chart, sending a 2028 first-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for Brown and giving Doubs, the former Packer, a four-year, $68 million contract as an unrestricted free agent. Brown, Pop Douglas , Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams are the receivers on the current 53-man roster. The team also signed former Dolphins receiver Ryan Miller to its practice squad Monday, joining three other receivers -- Chandler Brayboy (first year, Elon), Kyle Dixon (rookie, Culver-Stockton) and Cameron Dorner (rookie, North Texas).

stories.title: What placing Romeo Doubs on IR means for the Patriots
stories.summary: The veteran wide receiver will be out for at least the next four weeks.
stories.detailText: Romeo Doubs’ sixth game as a member of the New England Patriots was a brief affair. The offseason signing played only two snaps, the second of which a 42-yard touchdown catch that saw him remain down with a shoulder injury. The ailment kept him out of the remainder of the game, and will now sideline him for a minimum of four additional contests: as the team announced on Monday, Doubs has been placed on injured reserve . This means the Patriots will be without their high-prized free agency signing against the Chicago Bears, Miami Dolphins, Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, if not longer. What else does the move mean for New England? Let’s assess. Momentum stalled Doubs started his Patriots tenure with an underwhelming performance in Seattle, but he has since managed to turn a corner and develop a nice rapport with quarterback Drake Maye. Including his one reception on Sunday against the New York Jets, he now sits at 14 catches that he took for a team-leading 261 yards and three touchdowns. His 18.6 yards per catch rank second behind only Kyle Williams’ 24.5 and his 11 first downs are third, trailing Hunter Henry’s 13 and DeMario Douglas’ 12. For at least the next four games, however, Doubs will not be able to add to those numbers. He also will not be able to continue building his chemistry with Maye, which looked promising in recent weeks. Wide receiver turnover continues The Patriots just activated A.J. Brown off injured reserve after his four-week stint on the list due to a high ankle sprain, but the team’s new-found depth at wide receiver was short-lived. The pair shared just two snaps together before Doubs was lost to injury. The shoulder issue that will keep him out for at least the next four games is the latest blow to New England’s continuity at the position. Two weeks ago, Mack Hollins was also sent to IR due to a calf injury he sustained in the team’s win in Buffalo; he will be eligible to return after the Week 8 game in Miami. And so, for the time being, New England’s receiver group looks like this: 53-man roster (4): A.J. Brown (1), DeMario Douglas (3), Kyle Williams (18 | KR), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad (4): Kyle Dixon (83), Cameron Dorner (88), Chandler Brayboy (81), Ryan Miller (—) IR (2): Romeo Doubs (87), Mack Hollins (13), Jeremiah Webb (29 | season-ending) The Patriots played one game under similar circumstances so far: in Week 5 against the Raiders, they also only had four wide receivers on their active roster. Back then, the team actually opted not to elevate any extra depth. from the practice squad and instead relied on the tight end position — especially rookie Eli Raridon — to help pick up the slack. New England might use a similar approach in the near future, and at least until Mack Hollins is eligible for a return. Pressure on A.J. Brown A.J. Brown’s first game back from injured reserve was a disappointment. He did catch three passes for 27 yards, but did so on 10 total targets while also dropping two would-be touchdowns. With Doubs now out, the Patriots will need him to be better. While Brown alone won’t have to carry the load offensively, he might be the single most important X-factor when it comes to New England maintaining its current form on that side of the ball. If he can step up, the transition from Doubs to him as WR1 should go rather smoothly, despite the two being different player types; if not, the team could be running into some problems in the very near future. Despite his underwhelming comeback, the Patriots are optimistic. “A.J. has high expectations for himself, and we have high expectations for him as well,” said head coach Mike Vrabel on Sunday. “[I’m] confident that he’ll come back, do a lot of things and help us here the rest of the season.” Bad injury luck continues The Patriots have been decimated by injuries this year, and just six weeks into the season have already been forced to rely on their depth at multiple spots in the lineup. On offense alone, they are currently without fullback Reggie Gilliam, wide receivers Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins, tight end Julian Hill, and right guard Mike Onwenu, plus his replacement among the starters, Greg Van Roten. They also saw A.J. Brown miss four games, both left tackle Will Campbell and running back TreVeyon Henderson get shaken up a week ago. In addition, there are question marks over three O-linemen — Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown — after they were unable to finish the Jets game on Sunday. In total, the Patriots have now placed 20 different players on injured reserve dating back to Hill’s season-ending injury in the offseason. That does not include Harold Landry and Brenden Schooler spending time on the PUP and NFI lists, respectively, nor others such as Christian Gonzalez or Craig Woodson missing time due to injury. Long story short, it has been a challenging season so far for the Patriots and continues to be just that. Salary cap changes As part of the four-year, $68 million contract he signed with the Patriots in March, Doubs agreed to per-game roster bonuses totaling $1.7 million. At least four installments of those bonuses totaling $400,000 will not be earned now while he is on injured reserve. Considering that those bonuses were classified as likely to be earned after he played all 17 games for the Packers last season, the Patriots are set to receive a credit on their 2027 salary cap. Doubs’ cap number for next season will therefore decrease by $400,000 or more, depending on how much time he will actually end up missing either on IR or as a game-day inactive. Unless there are any adjustments, that number is currently set to be no higher than $18.2 million. Furthermore, Doubs might have some trouble getting his up to $3 million in not-likely-to-be-earned contract incentives for this season . He has $750,000 each on the line for 70 catches, 80 catches, 1,000 receiving yards and 1,200 receiving yards. His currently-projected 2027 cap number will only change in case he does manage to unlock those incentive escalators. Favorable timing It may be the dimmest of silver linings, but the timing of Doubs’ trip to injured reserve actually works out relatively well for the Patriots. With their bye coming up after the Lions game in Germany — i.e. the fourth and theoretically final game he will miss — they would have an extra week to get him up to speed before actually playing another game. Yes, we are grasping at straws here, thanks for asking. Opportunity earned Doubs’ spot on the 53-man roster went to safety Elliott Davison, who was elevated from the practice squad to the game day team each of the last two weeks. With now six safeties on the active roster, this gives New England some extra depth in the secondary and flexibility with nickel and dime packages as well as on special teams: 53-man roster (6): Kevin Byard (31), Craig Woodson (4), Jaylen Reed (23), Brenden Schooler (41), Mike Brown (33), Elliott Davison (27) IR (1): Dell Pettus (24) For Davison, who had one practice squad elevation left, the move also comes with a serious bay pump. After earning a weekly salary of $13,750 on the developmental team, he is now up to $49,166.67 — a 258% increase.

stories.title: Jalen Hurts expected to miss season after blood clots discovered in QB's lungs
stories.summary: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs, according to NFL Network and ESPN.
stories.detailText: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback's lungs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter. Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for at least three months, sources informed of the diagnosis told Rapoport and Schefter. Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs. Hurts is "clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations," according to the statement, but will not be allowed to participate in football activities while on anticoagulation medication. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery," the statement said. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects." Hurts was initially diagnosed with what was described as a superficial blood clot in his calf. That diagnosis occurred in London before the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Hurts played in that game -- a 19-17 loss for the Eagles -- despite the initial diagnosis and attempted 40 passes. Sources told Rapoport that Hurts was in the hospital in London until 4 a.m. on the morning of the game. He did not sleep the night before the game because he was told that sleeping posed health risks associated with the clot, according to sources. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni did not go into detail about why Hurts was allowed to play in the Jaguars game after he was diagnosed with having a blood clot but maintained that "the health of our players is always at the forefront of our mind" while expressing "full faith" in the team's medical experts. "The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys, to help them," Sirianni said Monday. Hurts' clot is considered to be "provoked" -- meaning a favorable prognosis with treatment and care -- because he was cleated in his calf, sources told Rapoport. The Eagles placed Hurts on injured reserve two days ago after consultations with numerous doctors and experts. Hurts already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers , but the Eagles waited to make the roster move until after consulting with medical experts, according to sources. Tanner McKee started in Hurts' place Sunday, completing 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and a touchdown in Philadelphia's 25-14 home loss to Carolina. Sirianni would not reveal the contents of his personal conversations with Hurts but acknowledged it will be a transition not having Hurts on the field for the foreseeable future. "I haven't been without Jalen for an extended period of time. I have the utmost confidence in Tanner but I miss him. I miss him and I know that will be the case because Jalen and I have been together, head coach and quarterback, for six years so that's natural." "I don't want to speak for him in any sense of the matter but I deeply care about him and hope that he continues to improve with what he's going through." Hurts took a cleat to his calf area on Oct. 4 against the Los Angeles Rams . He informed the Eagles' medical staff of the injury after practice on Oct. 8. and was back at practice the next day before the team left for London. An ultrasound in London on Oct. 10 revealed Hurts' superficial blood clot. The Eagles said last week that their medical staff and London-based doctors reviewed the ultrasound results and "concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play" against the Jaguars. After returning to Philadelphia, Hurts underwent a follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday that revealed movement in the blood clot, prompting the Eagles to rule him out for the game against the Panthers. Hurts hadn't missed more than two games in a season since becoming Philadelphia's quarterback in 2021. He is the fourth-leading passer in franchise history and has led the Eagles to three NFC East titles, two Super Bowl appearances and a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs two years ago in Super Bowl LIX, when he was named MVP. ESPN's Tim McManus contributed to this report.

stories.title: 3 keys to a 49ers win over the Commanders: Can Raheem Morris contain Jayden Daniels?
stories.summary: The Niners have a favorable matchup at home on Monday night.
stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers in action during the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have a chance to go 6-0 on Monday night when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi’s Stadium in primetime. Heading into the game, the 49ers are 7.5-point favorites on a hefty 51.5 point total. San Francisco has been on a heater to start the year, and they’ve had success over some quality opponents so far. The Niners have blown out the Los Angeles Rams and Miami Dolphins. They beat the Arizona Cardinals, who have looked more competitive than expected this year. And they’ve beaten the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, who were both in their respective conference championship games last year. They’re taking on a Commanders team coming off an embarrassing loss, as a last-second blunder by quarterback by quarterback Jayden Daniels forced them into a tie with the New York Giants last weekend. San Francisco does have some injury news going into the game, as receiver Mike Evans is expected to play despite missing the entire week of practice. How can they pull off the win on Monday night? Here are three keys to a Niners win in Week 6. Maintain third down efficiency The 49ers have been the second-most efficient offense in the NFL through Week 6, ranking only behind the Buffalo Bills in EPA per play. A big part of that has been winning on early downs. They’re by far the most efficient offense on the league by EPA per play on first and second downs. As a result, they don’t get to third downs that often, ranking 32nd in the NFL in third downs per game. The Commanders have actually been quite a solid early-down defense, ranking eighth in the NFL in EPA allowed per play on first and second downs. However, when you get to third downs, it’s a different story. Washington is 28th in the NFL on third downs by EPA allowed per play. They struggle to get off the field, ranking 24th in the NFL in third down conversion rate allowed (43.2 percent). The 49ers have regularly been an elite third-down conversion team under Kyle Shanahan, and they lead the NFL in conversion rate this year, while ranking second in success rate on third downs. This is setting up to be a strong environment for the 49ers offense, and the total indicates so. The numbers are on their side here in this matchup with both early down, and especially third-down success. Contain the quarterback Washington’s offensive line has been better than expected this year, and the Commanders have shown they want to run the ball as well. The issue? They’ve been inefficient in doing so. But with Jayden Daniels back, Washington’s run game saw a boost last weekend, with the quarterback going for over 100 yards and two touchdowns on the ground alone. The 49ers will be in a good spot if they can continue stopping the run on Monday. But a big part of the equation is accounting for Daniels’s feet too, which is what makes the passing game more dangerous as well with the scramble drills. Raheem Morris has been creative getting pressure on the quarterback this year. This could be more of a contain game for the 49ers’ defensive line, and stopping the run on early downs will also help mitigate the threat of Daniels and force Washington into unfavorable situations. Get off to a strong start The 49ers have had a couple of impressive finishes to games this season, thanks to some clutch play from Brock Purdy. The MVP candidate engineered some fourth-quarter scoring drives to win games against both Denver and Seattle, and the 49ers are 6-0 as a result. He also helped shutdown Arizona’s late comeback effort in Week 3, leading to the 36-30 win. San Francisco has shown they can win early. But getting off to a strong start here feels like a big key. One, we just mentioned Washington’s struggles running the ball. Playing from behind for a large portion of the game would only make them even more one-dimensional. Two, the Niners remain banged up at receiver, and Mike Evans is clearly hurt coming into this one. Even against a shoddy Commanders pass defense, it would be ideal if the 49ers didn’t have to rely as much on Evans and his banged-up self in a game where they’re favored by 7.5 points. We also saw the run game start coming to life against Seattle. Remaining balance feels like the way to solve this Commanders defense, and the 49ers have been highly efficient this season when they’ve been able to. The Niners are at home here as big favorites. The matchup plays into their favor, and it feels like a spot where they should take care of business, rather than letting things linger against a dangerous quarterback.

stories.title: Davante Adams to miss 6-10 weeks with hamstring injury
stories.summary: Adams ruptured his hamstring in Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals; will this end his career?
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams will place receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring that he suffered at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, according to Sean McVay. The receiver will miss between 6-10 weeks, which opens up the possibility that Adams will not return to the team this season. If that is the case, have we seen the last of Davante Adams in the NFL? In addition, the Rams announced that Poona Ford is out for the year with a torn triceps, and Kobie Turner will miss 4-6 weeks with a groin injury. Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that WR Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and now will be sidelined 6-10 weeks. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 Adams came up limping on a non-contact injury on Sunday, moments before the Rams scored a go-ahead touchdown in the final minute. The team did not give any information on what happened to Adams or the extent of his injury after the game, until McVay’s comments on Monday that now point to an extended absence for star receiver. In six games, Adams caught 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns. That includes over 300 yards and two touchdowns in the two games that Puka Nacua missed due to a core injury. The Rams will have to turn to other options now, which could include an increased role for Tutu Atwell , but also Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, and sixth-round rookie C.J. Daniels. L.A. has largely kept their passing offense contained to Puka, Adams, and Tyler Higbee lately. The team’s other tight ends have not been productive in the passing game and second-year pro Terrance Ferguson is also on IR. Adams is a free agent in 2027 after completing a two-year, $44 million contract he signed in 2025. The Rams signed Aaron Donald to boost an already-stout defensive line, but now they lose Ford and Turner with Myles Garrett already on injured reserve. Turner is a free agent in 2027, making his case for an extension even more complicated. Ford was a run-stopper only and now L.A. must rely on players like Tyler Davis and Ty Hamilton to step up next week. Donald has not been the player he was before, even at the tail end, so now is the time for him to bring back a bit of that magic.

LaFleur didn't rule anything out for Week 8 even though the Packers will have a quick turnaround to a Thursday game against the Panthers. “I think there are things you can do on a short week if you've got a guy like that to get him primed and ready to go," LaFleur said. "He's gotta clear some hurdles before we get to that point." Parsons said last week that he want to do all he can to avoid any kind of "overcompensation injury" upon his return and that would seem to work against the idea of returning during a week with little actual practice time. The Packers would then have a little more time to ramp Parsons up to a Week 9 game against the Patriots, but any thoughts of seeing him in the lineup will have to wait for that first step back on the practice field.

stories.title: Eagles-Panthers snap counts
stories.summary: Week 6 playing time tracker.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Darius Cooper #80 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs against the Carolina Panthers during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Jordan Mailata is the only player on offense who’s played 100% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps this season. He’s also played 11.32% of the Eagles’ special teams snaps. Well, the Eagles did have offensive line continuity in this game with the same lineup from last week and none of the starters getting hurt in this game. Not that it really made a difference for the offense. Tanner McKee posted a 77.5 passer rating in his first career start in a game where the Eagles weren’t resting starters. He wasn’t good and neither was his support system (coaching and talent combined). With Carson Steele suffering a shoulder injury, Dameon Pierce nearly had to play the entire game. The Eagles dressed Jaydon Blue, who was called up from the practice squad, but clearly did not trust him to play. Pierce has logged 10 targets combined over the last two games. Makai Lemon has logged the highest snap count percentages of his rookie season in back-to-back games. He saw the third-most targets on Sunday with six. They resulted in three catches for 19 yards. DeVonta Smith clearly wasn’t 100% while playing through a hamstring injury. Despite seeing more limited snaps than usual, he led the Eagles with 14 targets, which produced seven receptions for 75 yards and a touchdown. Dontayvion Wicks was also not 100% while playing through a hamstring injury. He saw the fifth-most targets on the team. There have been calls for Darius Cooper to play more. And not just from me! He’s the team’s best blocking receiver and he was coming off a career receiving performance in Week 5. And how was he rewarded? With the fifth-most snaps of any pass-catcher and just two targets, the same amount as Elijah Moore and Carson Steele. And this despite the fact that McKee and Cooper have worked well together in the past! Not to mention Smith and Wick playing through injuries. Just seems like the coaching staff could’ve done a better job of trying to get one of their more inspiring offensive options at the moment more involved. “[The Eagles] can't be taking Darius Cooper off the field. Darius Cooper, I would argue, might be their second-most important receiver for the way they want to play." — @FDuffyNFL pic.twitter.com/01198zpjpg — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 12, 2026 PHLY’s Bo Wulf pointed out that Johnny Mundt leads the NFL in holding penalties at his position. Hasn’t exactly been a great addition to the tight end room. Elijah Moore logged his first touch in an Eagles uniform; a single reception for four yards. DEFENSE Yet another game where the defense had to be on the field a lot because the offense simply can’t sustain drives. The Eagles’ defense has faced the third-most snaps in the NFL this season and they’re not very far behind the teams ahead of them. This was Jalen Carter’s second-highest snap count percentage of the season, only behind Week 1. This jibes with the sentiment that he’s getting healthier. Though it’s not really ideal to be playing him this much. He played 36 more snaps than the next-closest defensive tackle! With Jalyx Hunt unable to play in this game, Nolan Smith getting hurt early on, and Jonathan Greenard clearly playing through injury, Arnold Ebiketie was the Eagles’ top edge rusher. Keyshawn James-Newby went from being a temporary practice squad elevation to the Eagles’ No. 2 edge rusher in this game due to all of the injuries at that position. Kenny Moore, not Marcus Epps, was the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages. Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. rotated at off-ball linebacker but it wasn’t exactly a 50-50 split. Jordan Davis logged his second-highest snap count of the season and that was with him getting injured in the fourth quarter. He was credited with half of a sack, which gives him half of a sack on the season. Byron Young playing the same amount of snaps as Moro Ojomo? Not really what you want to see. But Ojomo did get banged up. Again, Greenard was clearly limited coming into this game. Ty Robinson played more often than usual and actually logged a pressure on just five pass rush snaps! Perhaps he warrants some more playing time. SPECIAL TEAMS Making his NFL regular season debut, rookie safety Cole Wisniewski was limited to special teams duty after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Marcus Epps was limited to special teams duty in his first game back from injury. This after beginning the season as the safety next to Mukuba in nickel packages. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Cole Payton, Jaydon Blue, Drew Kendall INACTIVE: Marquise Brown, Joe Milton III, Saquon Barkley, Michael Carter II, A.J. Epenesa, Jalyx Hunt, Lane Johnson Payton served as QB2 behind McKee. A little curious to have Blue active but not use him at all to spell Pierce. Blue is relatively newer to the team but he’s been in Philly since the last day of August. Kendall was active on an emergency depth basis. Perhaps he’ll be healthy enough to replace Jake Majors in Week 7. Hollywood Brown missed three games due to injury and then was a healthy scratch behind six active receivers. I can’t imagine he’s on this roster for much longer? Can’t imagine he has much trade value but maybe Howie Roseman tries to hold out hope on that front? And then maybe cuts him after the trade deadline, if not sooner? Milton III was designated as the emergency third quarterback after only joining the Eagles on Friday. Barkley, MC2, Epenesa, and Hunt all missed the game due to injury. There seems to be hope that Barkley might be able to play in Week 7. As a reminder, Johnson is set to remain on the Eagles’ roster until June 2027 , even though he retired.

stories.title: Rams WR Davante Adams will miss 6-10 weeks with ruptured hamstring, Sean McVay says
stories.summary: Adams appeared to injure himself on the final drive of Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams will be without star wide receiver Davante Adams for quite some time. In a press conference on Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that Adams ruptured his hamstring. He will be out six to 10 weeks with the injury. Adams appeared to injure himself on the final drive of Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals: The 33-year-old receiver pulled up suddenly and started hopping in the back of the end zone, before limping off the field. The Cardinals won the game with a late rally and a walk-off field goal. Rams HC Sean McVay announced WR Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and will be out 6-10 weeks. pic.twitter.com/Z8acRYddM0 — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 19, 2026 Adams leads the Rams in receiving yards so far this season, and was a key part of the team’s offense with players like Puka Nacua missing time at the start of the year. In six games, Adams had racked up 480 receiving yards and four touchdowns. A six-week recovery would see Adams returning to the field sometime in December, while 10 could mean the receiver would be back in time for the last two regular-season games in January. Given the timeline, the Rams will likely place Adams on injured reserve. Adams is one of four significant injuries that McVay announced on Monday: Defensive tackle Poona Ford is out for the year with a tricep injury, while DT Kobie Turner is headed to injured reserve with a groin injury. Kicker Blake Grupe, who just signed with the team last week, is also out for the season with a knee injury after he attempted a tackle early in Sunday’s game. The loss to Arizona dropped the Rams to 2-4, a stunning turn of events for a team that was heavily touted ahead of the regular season.

stories.title: Cowboys' Stephen Jones 'absolutely' supports Brian Schottenheimer after another miserable showing, 2-4 start
stories.summary: A former under Schottenheimer with the Jets, meanwhile, blasted him as a "mid OC."
stories.detailText: Another disastrous Sunday for the Dallas Cowboys has led into another Monday of chatter around what's wrong with the team. The focus continues to swirl around head coach Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys produced a surprisingly tepid offensive effort in a 23-13 loss to the Packers on national TV Sunday night . On the heels of a 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers in Week 5, it marked the second poor outing for an offensive unit that's been viewed as a strength of a team that now sits at 2-4. The run game ranks 31st out of 32 teams with 76 yards per game, and a normally prolific pass game anchored by quarterback Dak Prescott has accounted for two touchdowns and four interceptions in the last two games. Adding to the concern is that the return of All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith from injury the last two weeks has coincided with the team's offensive struggles. The heat continues to rise under Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Kevin Sabitus via Getty Images Stephen Jones 'absolutely' supports Schottenheimer Schottenheimer is a former offensive coordinator and the offensive play-caller for the Cowboys in addition to being the team's head coach. With the new-found concerns around the Cowboys' offense, all questions about the team's struggles point to him. Cowboys COO Stephen Jones, the son of team owner Jerry Jones, made an appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday to talk Cowboys football. He, of course, was asked if the team maintained its confidence in Schottenheimer as head coach. His answer was unequivocal. "Absolutely. There's not any question in Jerry's and [my] mind," Jones said. "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. "Feel really good as I've mentioned throughout this conversation about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to have it evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games." In 38 years of ownership under Jerry Jones, the Cowboys have largely been hesitant to make coaching moves amid outside pressure to do so, particularly during the season. This appears to be the company line with Schottenheimer, whose seat apparently is not as hot internally as the Cowboys' record would suggest. Jones admits 'surprising' offensive struggles Stephen Jones reiterated throughout his interview Monday that the Cowboys "like our coaching staff" while acknowledging the obvious concerns on both sides of the ball. "We probably had an unrealistic view of how fast we could get the defense turned around," Jones said. … "The surprising thing is we were playing so well on offense. All of last year, we played good offense and then certainly played well to start the season. And these last two games it is surprising in terms of how we're performing on offense. "Our running game just hasn't come together this year up to this point. We certainly feel like we've got the players in our offensive line group and our running back." Former player under Schottenheimer blasts Cowboys coach While Jones says he's confident in his head coach, a former player under Schottenheimer is anything but. Former NFL wide receiver Braylon Edwards played under Schottenheimer when Schottenheimer was the offensive coordinator of the New York Jets. The Jets lost consecutive AFC championship games in the 2009 and 2010 seasons. They scored 17 and 19 points in those games, respectively. Edwards has been watching the Cowboys, and he blames Schottenheimer for those poor offensive outings in the Jets' title game losses. Watching the @dallascowboys struggle two weeks in a row reminded me of why we as a Jets offense were terrible in back to back afc championship games in '09' and '10'....mid OC by the name of Brian Schottenheimer. — Braylon Edwards (@OfficialBraylon) October 19, 2026 "Watching the Dallas Cowboys struggle two weeks in a row reminded me of why we as a Jets offense were terrible in back to back afc championship games in '09' and '10,'" Edwards tweeted Monday. "mid OC by the name of Brian Schottenheimer." Edwards has held that grudge for 16 years and pounced on the opportunity of the Cowboys' struggles to air it Monday. And he certainly speaks for the frustrations of some of the Cowboys fan base. Thanks to an NFC East that doesn't appear to have any good teams that's led by the 3-2-1 New York Giants, the Cowboys can reasonably project to rally and win the division. But they're under pressure to turn things around now. They'll face the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles next Monday in a third straight prime-time game with a national TV audience. If they don't get the job done then, it will became that much harder for Cowboys brass to continue to voice their support for Schottenheimer.

stories.title: Commanders place starting RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on IR
stories.summary: The Washington Commanders placed running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve, sidelining their starting back for at least four games.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The Washington Commanders placed running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve, sidelining their starting back for at least four games. Croskey-Merritt reinjured his groin in the team's Week 5 tie vs. the New York Giants . He originally hurt it in training camp, sidelining him for the final two preseason games. The good news for Washington (1-3-1) is that corner Trey Amos , who fractured his left fibula in Week 9 last season, was activated off IR ahead of Monday's game against the 49ers (5-0). Amos was Washington's most effective corner in the nine games he started as a rookie in 2025. He recovered from the broken leg, but entering camp he was placed on the physically unable to perform list because of a soft tissue/muscle soreness. He injured an ankle in his first practice this summer and was placed on IR to open the season. Croskey-Merritt is Washington's leading rusher this season with 239 yards, and he has also scored twice. In 2025, he led the Commanders with 805 rushing yards as a rookie. After averaging 4.6 yards per carry in his first season, he's gaining only 3.6 this year. Washington activated Jeremy McNichols off IR. He had injured a quad in training camp. His return will help a group that also includes Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler . The Commanders' run game ranks seventh in the NFL at 4.7 yards per carry. But a lot of that success is due to quarterbacks Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota . Washington leads the NFL with 268 yards rushing by its quarterbacks, and Daniels scored on runs of 38 and 26 yards vs. the Giants last week. Washington also placed backup outside linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste on injured reserve with pectoral injury. The Commanders activated backup inside linebacker Jordan Magee off IR. He'll bolster special teams.

stories.title: Patriots place wide receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve amid series of moves
stories.summary: The veteran sustained a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown catch.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Romeo Doubs #87 of the New England Patriots scores a touchdown against Brandon Stephens #21 of the New York Jets during the first quarter at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots will be without Romeo Doubs for a minimum of four games. The organization placed the veteran wide receiver on injured reserve amid a series of transactions announced Monday afternoon. Doubs, 26, sustained a shoulder injury while catching a 42-yard touchdown in the first quarter of Sunday’s 26-19 AFC East win at Gillette Stadium and was downgraded from questionable to out. The March signing stands with 14 receptions for 261 yards and three visits to the end zone this fall for an active depth chart that moves forward with A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. He has handled 246 offensive snaps through six games, including a pair of starts, and will not be eligible for a return until late November. Entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at No. 132 overall out of Nevada, Doubs spent the previous four campaigns with the Green Bay Packers. The 6-foot-2, 210-pound wideout’s career spans 216 catches for 2,685 yards and 24 touchdowns through 65 appearances. Taking the open spot on the 53-man roster in Foxborough, safety Elliott Davison has been promoted from the practice squad after twice serving as a standard elevation for matchups against the Las Vegas Raiders and New York Jets. Davison, 24, was scheduled to revert on Monday. The 6-foot, 190-pound safety has recorded two tackles and one pass deflection through his consecutive call-ups while playing 10 snaps on defense and 37 snaps on special teams. Signed to the Patriots’ practice squad in September before being released and re-signed , Davison originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025. The former UTSA defensive back spent the duration of his rookie year on the practice squad of the New Orleans Saints. New England also officially signed wide receiver Ryan Miller, center Jacob Rizy and guard Andrew Rupcich to the practice squad on Monday. The club released cornerback D’Shawn Jamison to make room among the 17-man group. Miller, 26, went undrafted out of Furman in 2023. The 6-foot-2, 217-pound wideout spent three seasons between the 53-man roster and practice squad of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being claimed off waivers by the New York Giants last December. Awarded to the Miami Dolphins amid training camp and let go last week, Miller has played in 30 NFL games, including six starts, while totaling 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. He scored his most recent TD in September from 77 yards away. Rizy, 24, began 2026 on New England’s practice squad after arriving as part of the organization’s undrafted class in May. The 6-foot-5, 306-pound rookie free agent played 155 snaps at center through three preseason games and was waived ahead of the league’s 53-man roster deadline. A former second-team and first-team All-Ivy League selection, Rizy spent three years at Harvard and two years at Florida State. The 27-game starter logged time at center, left guard, right guard and right tackle during his collegiate run. Rupcich, 27, had been waived by the Patriots with an injury settlement in August after reverting to injured reserve. The 6-foot-6, 325-pound Culver-Stockton alum now circles back to an offensive line that saw three starters in Ben Brown, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Morgan Moses ruled out on Sunday. Rupcich first joined New England’s practice squad last September and was retained on a futures contract in February. He entered the NFL with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022 and appeared in 12 games while in the AFC South, notching two starts. Jamison, 27, worked out and joined the Patriots’ practice squad last week before becoming a corresponding move amid the attrition. The 5-foot-9, 185-pound cornerback went undrafted out of Texas in 2023 and made his initial NFL stops with the San Francisco 49ers, Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers. He spent the first month of the 2026 season on the practice squad of the Arizona Cardinals. Jamison has appeared in 18 games while seeing 107 snaps on defense and 166 snaps on special teams. His career includes 10 tackles, one pass deflection and one start. The Chicago Bears host head coach Mike Vrabel’s 4-2 team at Soldier Field on Thursday. Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET.

stories.title: Rams’ investments in tight ends isn’t paying off
stories.summary: The Rams have five tight ends, but snap counts tell an flattering picture of them
stories.detailText: In a dull, lackluster Sunday matinee performance, the Los Angeles Rams dropped a second straight home heartbreaker, falling 16-15 to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday . L.A. came into the game as the NFL’s top yardage-producing offense, but left in a confused state, without a confident identity. Are they a building around a power run game, using between the tackles duo/inside zone concepts and attacking through the air with under-center play action? Or sitting back in shotgun formation and throwing the football 68% (the last four games) of the time in an underneath quick-read attack? When asked about the team’s identity at the post-game presser, Sean McVay said: “We’re figuring it out, I can’t answer that right now…” The Rams have Matthew Stafford, a gunslinger at quarterback and have thrown 20+% of passes at or behind the line of scrimmage in the these two consecutive losses. More importantly, they don’t mesh like an integral part of the offense, spreading it around to get playmakers the ball in space or taking advantage of numerical advantages over defenders. Maybe it’s a rhetorical question, but can the Rams realistically boast of another playmaker besides Puka Nacua? Going into the season, McVay’s offense was seen as the evolutionary next step in 13 personnel and tight end development. Instead, the Rams sputtered against one of the worst defenses in the NFL on Sunday and tight ends combined for nine catches on 10 targets with 53 yards, one touchdown, and a critical lost fumble by Tyler Higbee. If you’re reading this you have more fantasy points than Tyler Higbee pic.twitter.com/2KZ6NTbchY — betr (@betr) October 18, 2026 The Rams entered the season with five tight ends, including second-round picks in 2025 and 2026. The Rams enter Week 7 with Higbee’s 246 yards eclipsing the combined total of all four other tight ends (181 yards between Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson, and Max Klare) and he was supposed to be the one taking a step back. Higbee had the most tight end snaps for the team on Sunday, followed by Parkinson, who has just 55 yards in six games despite a $9 million salary cap hit. Ferguson is on IR. Klare is an occasional special teamer with one snap on offense. Can this get better? Fans have seen this before in the past, the offense compressing the passing game into the underneath areas too often and the run game becoming an afterthought. The antidote is complicated and would take discipline. Staying with the run game and using play action could loosen things up. Another thought is re-visiting the past, making the opposition defend the whole field again, both width and length, particularly the middle of the field against deep zones. Identify some secondary playmakers to give the offense variety, Nacua is a generational player, but a healthy offense needs more options. The McVay offense used to dictate the flow of the game, alternately taking the full time to snap the ball and going up tempo, L.A. appears to have gotten away from this. A good example is how the Rams have performed offensively in the fourth quarter of 2026 games. A quicker pace has led them to charting 40 percent of their total season yardage and scoring 43 percent of their total points in the final stanza. Sitting at 2-4 and staring up from last place in the division is not time to control and keep the offense in a grip, trying to gut out wins, it’s time to play like there’s nothing left to lose. Here’s a look at the snap count review from Sunday, players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (58, 100%) Is Staff the problem or the solution? Time to cut bait on the season and go with Ty Simpson or should the Rams circle the wagons until the bye week before making such a big decision? While the latter seems the most judicious path, the offense needs to unhook the brakes and let it rip until then. Staff can still bring it, as proven by his fourth quarter work this season. The game plan has to to be faster and less predictable. Running back Kyren Williams (42, 72%), Blake Corum (16, 28%) Although the run game showed the hint of being something to build on, the game plan goes away from it too quickly. As a duo, Williams and Corum put in solid work on Sunday, just would have liked to see them get more. A combined 92 yards rushing on 19 carries and five catches on eight targets. Williams had a drop and another tougher off-target attempt that hit of his hand. There was a lot of open field, had it connected. Blake Corum takes the screen pass into the end zone ‼️ AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8polUTpXGE — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Wide receiver Puka Nacua (52, 90%) , Davante Adams (43, 74%) Again, is Puka Nacua the Rams only offense? He is so damned tough and clutch, he demands the opposition to roll the defense his way, but he appears too often alone. Only three targets until five minutes left in the game is a criminal offense. Adams has proven that he still has something to contribute at 34. Hopefully that late-game foot injury is minor, the room is wafer thin. Konata Mumpfield (27, 47%), Jordan Whittington (8,14%) Creating a composite WR#3, Mumpfield and Whittington have been on the field for 285 of 410 offensive plays (70%) with 20 targets and 10 catches. Not a lot of return on investment on for an offense that wants to air it out. Tight end Colby Parkinson (36, 72%), Tyler Higbee (48, 83%), Davis Allen (18, 31%) The Rams have staked a lot on the use of multiple tight end formation, both money and draft capital. To this point, it’s fair to say that it hasn’t improved the the run game enough for the offense to lean into it. Nor has L.A. used it to attack downfield. As a group, they are averaging less than 10 yards per catch. Offensive line David Quessenberry, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (58, 100%) Quessenberry was a pleasant surprise on the blind side, most expected a disaster. With the Rams throwing so much, the line will give up some pressures. I see the biggest pass blocking problem as the Rams inability to adjust to blitz calls and Sunday was no different. Maybe it was unexpected, Arizona hadn’t blitzed much in the first five weeks. But it’s not a new problem, blitz calls, particularly delayed, have been a a burr under the L.A. saddle all year. We have seen Sand Deuce mostly vs. 3×1 this year, but here it is vs. 2×2. This is the blitz path of the year, teams have run it a ton through 6 weeks, and we will continue to see it https://t.co/yNWDkkvK0h pic.twitter.com/q9A7l5qes0 — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) October 19, 2026 Special teams P Ethan Evans, LS Joe Cardona, K Blake Grupe Talk about adding injury to insult. In his maiden Rams voyage, Grupe drills a mid-length field goal and because of poor coverage on the ensuing kickoff , is forced into a making a tackle as the fail-safe option and tweaks a knee. Evans was on the cusp of an outstanding punting game, he dropped two inside the the five and got good first bounces, but the cover team couldn’t cash in. You never hear much about Cardona, means he’s doing well as long snapper. Defensive interior Aaron Donald (42, 58%), Braden Fiske (36, 50%) Just an idea, the L.A. defensive braintrust could consider lining up up Aaron Donald or Braden Fiske out on the edge at 7T on a handful of reps per game. With the Rams deep rotation at DT, It would be very interesting to see AD and Fiske playing as at wide defensive end. Donald is starting to round into shape, showing his move skills and making impact plays against both run and pass. Fiske played well, particularly on the move, but can get washed out by bigger, stronger offensive linemen when trying to hold ground. Kobie Turner (23, 32%), Pooona Ford (25, 35%), Tyler Davis (28, 39%), Ty Hamilton (18, 25%) The interior wasn’t bad per se against the Cardinals, but they did allow Arizona to control the game on the ground. While the unit as a whole, seems less stout than 2025, it feels as if Ford and Davis are having less of an impact clogging up run lanes. That’s important because neither offer a lot of pass rush. Interestingly, Turner was hardly noticed and it was his lowest usage as a pro. No reports on his being nicked up. Hamilton had the most snaps of his two pro seasons, but didn’t move the needle much. Edge Byron Young (57, 79%) Had a good game solid vs both run and pass. Tough to create a lot of pressure when the opposing pass plan is predominantly underneath, one-read releases. Josaiah Stewart (55, 76%), Wesley Bailey (17, 24%), Desjuan Johnson (15, 21%) All three struggled setting the edge, but there doesn’t appear to be anywhere else to turn at this point. Stewart has some good reps, it’s just a case of his being better as a complimentary piece rather an every down player. I’m less sure each week of Wesley Bailey and Desjuan Johnson out there. Is it the best personnel grouping to consistently have them on the field together? Although they both hustle and give their all, Johnson already appeared to have taken a step back during preseason and Bailey is struggling with growing pains. Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (71, 99%), Omar Speights (21, 29%) Without the impact peanut punch reps, Landman is like Rams linebackers from the recent past, serviceable play overall, plenty of tackles three yards back from the line of scrimmage and not much offered in pass coverage. Speights played well early in the game, looked aggressive and attacked the ball in pursuit. Bounced off and missed a tackle in the 2nd quarter and didn’t see a lot of action after that. Safety Quentin Lake (72, 100%) Kamren Curl (72, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (48, 67%) Jaylen McCollough (32, 44%) I know it’s difficult to set him against a certain position player every snap with all the formational subterfuge these days, but Lake is a much better coverage player when lined up on tight ends, big and strong enough at the catch point and not out-matched athletically. His use on special teams doesn’t make a lot of sense, he doesn’t play aggressively on them. Curl had another consistent game. Kinchens took a shot at an INT early and just missed, other than that it was a quiet performance. After a couple of weeks on the outs at safety, McCollough was back in the mix. Four tackles and he landed a couple of hits you hear and feel through the TV screen. Cornerback Jaylen Watson (72, 100%), Josh Wallace (72,100%), Emmanuel Forbes (16, 22%) For a 2-4 team, the L.A. pass defense has been consistently good and was again Sunday. Even without the support of a strong pass rush, the corners have held up well. While McDuffie and Watson have been as advertised, the biggest surprise has been Wallace. While I think he’s best projected as a rotational safety, he’s improved at corner with more play time. Good tackler in space and shown he be fairly sticky in man coverage. Aside from McDuffie, opponents have been attacking the Rams corners lack of makeup speed with underneath crossing patterns, long developing across the field and through traffic. Opponents have found success in these situations. Are the Rams staring into the abyss? The Rams are ranked 3rd in total offense and 3rd in total defense this season They are the only team to be ranked top 5 in both They are 2-4, in last place in the NFC West pic.twitter.com/hROWMo83av — PFF (@PFF) October 19, 2026 There are plenty of scenarios on how the Rams can still get to the playoffs and I subscribe to them all, but do think that showing they can stack up a few wins is the best next course of action. Without that happening, starting next week, the season could easily be lost. Execution should be the buzz word for the future, both offense and defense. I would add special teams to the other units, but that right now, is unrealistic. While the offense seems without an identity and wildly inconsistent, the defense doesn’t rate any flowers either. The analytics and stat numbers are holding steady, but they were trampled under foot by the 49ers in the opener and couldn’t hold fourth quarter leads in the other three losses. Make the climb back to .500 and then fans can re-visit back door play off scenarios.

stories.title: Giants 'working through' starting quarterback situation after benching Jameis Winston
stories.summary: After benching Jameis Winston in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints Sunday afternoon, J.J. McCarthy nearly lead the team to a comeback win in his Giants debut.
stories.detailText: After benching Jameis Winston in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints Sunday afternoon and watching J.J. McCarthy nearly lead the team to a comeback win in his Giants debut, New York was left with an important question: Is it time to switch things up at quarterback once again, at least for Week 7? Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday afternoon that the team isn't sure of its next move just yet. "We're working through that now," he said. "Honing in on a decision" In his 11-plus minutes on the field, McCarthy spearheaded a 17-point rally which, though it fell just short, proved his ability to pull his team back into contention . The Big Blue have been battling a void at the QB position since Week 1, when starter Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury . Though they remain atop the NFC East, the team is just 3-2-1. In his five games so far this season, Winston has completed 90 of his 158 passes for 957 yards and seven touchdowns against five interceptions and 15 sacks. Two of those interceptions and four of those sacks came on Sunday. When asked what goes into making a decision like that, Harbaugh said it's a matter of considering the several factors that impact a game. "Like every other personnel decision we make, what gives us the best chance to win the football game at this given time, or what combination of players and schemes and things like that give us the best chance to move the ball, score points, protect the football, etc., so all the things that help us win," he said. "Whatever it is that furthers us and helps us, just to use the basic obvious point. That's what we want to do."

stories.title: Steelers 'excited' for NFL Paris game vs Saints despite spate of disruptive protests
stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers plan to leave Thursday evening ahead of the first NFL game in France against the New Orleans Saints.
stories.detailText: The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to monitor the unrest in and around Paris ahead of their NFL Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints on Oct. 25 at Stade de France , outside the city. Coach Mike McCarthy said everything has proceeded as planned so far, despite disruptive protests that have gripped France in recent weeks. And that conversations within the team continue as events continue to unfold on the ground. “The team is excited about playing over there,” he told reporters at his weekly news conference. “We’re in contact with the league. We had a Zoom call today with the league office, which is the normal protocol before you get over there. With the whole team. So we feel like we have a really good plan. We’re aware of the situation over there and have a lot of confidence in our plan.” Required reading: Steelers PFF grades: Germie Bernard shines; Troy Fautanu stagnates The Steelers plan to leave the United States on Thursday, so their stay in the country won’t be very long. The team followed a similar plan last season, when it faced the Minnesota Vikings in Dublin, Ireland . McCarthy said some team personnel have already arrived in the area in anticipation of the matchup. The Saints have already arrived in France. They departed the United States directly after their NFL Week 6 victory against the New York Giants and will spend the balance of the week across the Atlantic Ocean. NFL INTERNATIONAL GAMES: Full 2026 schedule, matchups and cities for every overseas game The league issued a statement Sunday, signaling that the game will proceed as planned for now. “Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday,” the league said. “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” MIKE MCCARTHY: Steelers coach misses halftime after 'freak' on-field injury At present, McCarthy and his coaching staff are more actively managing the disruption that the trans-Atlantic journey will cause to the weekly routine. Unlike last season, the Steelers won't get a bye after their international excursion and will face the Cleveland Browns on Nov. 1 back at Acrisure Stadium. So the focus has been on a plan to maximize the team’s competitiveness for both the Paris game itself and the subsequent AFC North division matchup. “Whether you’re playing in a Super Bowl or a Monday night game that’s more than five, six hours in the air, you look at all of those things,” McCarthy said. “The reality of it is, I’ve always just tried to stick to the basics. The hydration. The sleep. Just to make sure you give the men the best opportunity to prepare to perform, and then ultimately stay in as normal a flow of preparation as you can.” The Steelers picked up a 26-19 overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. They rallied from 13-0 and 16-3 deficits to earn their fourth win of the season and into a tie for the division lead with the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns at 4-2. stories.title: New problems surface as the Cowboys offense buckles under pressure
stories.summary: The Cowboys offense is suddenly a big problem
stories.detailText: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys provided another disappointing showing on Sunday night, losing to the Green Bay Packers, 23-13. The difficult part of this loss comes from the fact that the defense actually played okay. They struggled at times, which almost feels inevitable at this point, but they also gave their offense a fighting chance. The problem is that the Cowboys’ offense had no fight in them. What went wrong? To get a better sense of the issues in this game, let’s take a closer look at what happened in this game. The game started well with an eight-yard gain from Javonte Williams after Tyler Booker pushed into the second level with a great block. But a second-and-short became a third-and-long when Terence Steele completely whiffed on a block, and Williams was taken down in the backfield for a two-yard loss. This set up the first of what we would see all night, a Packers blitz getting in the face of Dak Prescott. Fortunately, Prescott read it quickly and fired a perfect pass to Ryan Flournoy to convert on third down. It was a good conversion. Things looked promising, but little did we know that those moments faded quickly. A minimal gain bootleg and running play set them up with another 3rd-and-4. The Packers again showed blitz, only this time the defenders dropped back into coverage. Prescott panicked and quickly swung it out to Williams, who had absolutely no chance. Just like that, the Cowboys’ first drive had stalled. After the Packers strolled 90 yards to take an early 7-0 lead, the offense needed to answer back, but what did they do instead? False start. Illegal man downfield. Right away, they are in a 1st-and-20 hole thanks to two penalties by the offensive line. After a couple of short checkdowns, the Cowboys came up short on third-and-long after facing yet another Packers blitz. The game had just started, and already we saw a big problem. The Packers’ defense had a good game plan. The Cowboys offense did not. In an unexpected turn, the defense came up with a huge takeaway, giving the ball back to Dallas in Packers territory. This was the break the team needed. Quickly, another tackle-for-loss running play puts them in another third down, but they convert. But after a first-down run went nowhere, the offense is forced to pass, and Prescott again came under fire. A linebacker blitz shook him after Prescott took a shot to the ribs. Then, a panicked Prescott didn’t see the defender drop back into coverage to jump a pass intended for CeeDee Lamb near the goal line. A chance for a game-tying touchdown turned into no points. After the pick, the Packers offense drove all the way down the field, however, the defense made a great goal line stand thanks to clutch defensive plays by Quinnen Williams and Malik Hooker. The Cowboys defense picked a great time to make their first stop on third down, and Green Bay had to settle for a field goal. The game was still within reason. The Cowboys offense then put together their best drive so far with a couple of decent runs and Dak throwing on the move. The best play from this series came when Prescott evaded a pass rusher and found George Pickens downfield. Finally, something good was about to happen. But no sooner did that feeling enter our souls than did it immediately escape when Lamb slipped coming out of his break, causing a perfectly thrown ball to go into the hands of a Packers defender. Once again, a red zone opportunity turns into a whole lotta nada for the Cowboys. The Packers offense again marched down the field with a well-executed two-minute drive finished off by a Jordan Love quarterback sneak. An entire half of football was played, and the Cowboys did not score a single point. It was 17-0, and the Packers got the ball to open the second half. The game was slipping away. In a surprise twist, the second half started fantastically. The Cowboys defense forced a quick three-and-out, and even sent the Packers backwards thanks to a Kenny Clark sack near the goal line. After a nice return from Jonathan Mingo, the Cowboys started their first possession of the second half inside Packers territory. The offense finally capitalized on an opportunity. It took a fourth-down conversion to Lamb, who had wisely changed his cleats, and some physical plays by Williams and Brevyn Spann-Ford, but the Cowboys punched it in, and suddenly they had life again. The mood started to shift, but we have seen this before. In fact, we have seen this quite a lot lately. The team starts slowly, falls into despair, and then finally shows some life and starts to climb back into the game. Was the stage set for another one of these dramatic comeback attempts? Could the defense honestly make enough stops to give their offense a chance? What happened next is hard to explain. The defense did give them a chance. The Packers never scored another touchdown. They kicked two field goals, putting them at 23 total points, but shockingly, that was more than enough to easily secure the victory for Green Bay. What had happened to the Cowboys’ offense? Their ensuing possessions looked eerily similar to what we saw early in the game. Can’t run the ball. Repeatedly throwing way short of the sticks. Blitz coming. Dak’s in trouble. It was a recurring nightmare. Prescott had to take what the defense gave up, constantly pulling up short. When he did go deeper, a defender was right in the hip pocket of the receiver, ready to come away with more interceptions. The running game had completely vanished, and the Cowboys always found themselves in third-and-long situations, allowing the Packers’ defense to pin their ears back and come after Dak. The Cowboys struggled to pick up where the Packers’ blitz was coming from as they disguised it very well. This caused us to repeatedly hear the announcer say, “Dak hit as he throws.” It felt like the Cowboys’ biggest gains came when Green Bay was tagged for roughing the passer, which happened three times. Dak was a sitting duck back there. It was really difficult to watch. Despite having two great receivers and a talented quarterback, the offense could not come up with anything. They did score a garbage-time touchdown with 44 seconds left in the game, but they could not land the two-point conversion, basically ending the game. The Cowboys need to figure out how to attack better in space. Based on what we have seen over the past two games, opposing defenses have picked up on tendencies and are exploiting areas that Dak and the offense are struggling with. And that is not going to end until the Cowboys offensive coaches come up with an effective counter. It is very unfortunate that the Cowboys wasted the best performance by the defense and gave away a very winnable game. Failing to execute when it is clear they have talent is a huge indicator that the coaching staff is failing them, and now it is no longer limited to just the defensive side of the ball.

stories.title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 6 win over the Cowboys
stories.summary: Digging into some numbers on the Packers Week 6 victory over the Cowboys
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6. Offense The Packers have switching up their personnel groupings quite a bit on a game-by-game basis, which I always like to see. Stay unpredictable. Become ungovernable. Against the Bears in Week 5 , we saw the Packers dial back their usage of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) quite a bit. In that game they were out of 11 personnel 54.2% of the time. This week they dialed that up: It was a good attack plan, as that personnel grouping was their best group while passing… …and while running. It’d be nice to get a rushing attack that could actually be decent, but the passing game has really improved as the offensive line has solidified. Who knew?! In this game, Jordan Love averaged 2.7 seconds to throw and had an ADOT (Average Depth of Target) of 9.7 yards. That’s a good, functional passing offense. That felt impossible only a few weeks ago. The Cowboys played primarily Cover 3 in this game, and Love shredded that coverage, going 10/14 for 142 yards (+0.38 EPA per Play). He also shredded the blitz, going 8/12 for 100 yards (+0.52 EPA per Play) when blitzed. The Packers pass rate of 62.9% feels about right. They would have been over 65% for the game if they didn’t take the air out of the ball in the 4th quarter (46.7% pass rate in the 4th). With as inept as the run game has looked this year I’d like to see that pass rate up just a bit, but hovering around 65% feels right with where this team currently is. Sure would be nice if Matthew Golden got his hands figured out (which is baffling, considering that seemed to be one of the stronger points in his game), but he still turned in a nice game. He notched 6 catches on 13 targets for 104 yards and a TD (+1.74 EPA per Reception). His average depth of target of 15.62 yards was 4.9 yards above the NFL average. Just imagine what his numbers would have looked like if he didn’t drop two TD passes. They continue to switch up their run attack depending on the opponent. They went about 50/50 this week, with 46.1% of their run game fitting into zone buckets and the rest into man/gap buckets. Did it work? Man, not really, but I like their attack plan. They’ve shown some improvement up front in terms of blocking, but the run game just hasn’t been good this year. Defense The Packers defense did a great job keeping the Cowboys offense off-balance all game, and they did that by generating pressure on Dak Prescott. Gannon has done a nice job at switching up defensive tendencies each week. This week the Packers blitzed on 35.71% of snaps, and generated pressure on 41.07% of dropbacks. Beyond blitzes, the stacked front looks bothered Prescott whether the Packers brought pressure or not. On the game, Prescott wasn’t good whether he was blitzed (-0.16 EPA per Play) or not blitzed (-0.24 EPA per Play). Those numbers would look even better for the Packers defense if they didn’t get hit with a couple pretty ticky-tack roughing the passer calls. In terms of passing zones, Prescott had a couple underneath zones he had success throwing to, but there’s a lot of red in this chart. Dani Dennis-Sutton continues to show up every week. This week he had a pressure rate of 22.7% (8.56% above NFL average), with an average time to pressure of 2.67 seconds. Albums listened to: Eels – Cookie Happened

Croskey-Merritt was ruled out of Monday night's game against the 49ers on Saturday because of the injury and the Commanders placed him on injured reserve on Monday afternoon. The move leaves Austin Ekeler, Rachaad White, and Jeremy McNichols as the available backs for Washington. McNichols is a new addition to the roster. He was activated from injured reserve on Monday along with cornerback Trey Amos and linebacker Jordan Magee. All three players were listed as questionable, but now carry no injury designation. The Commanders opened up two other roster spots by placing linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste on injured reserve and waiving linebacker Austin Keys. Linebacker T.J. Maguranyanga was elevated from the practice squad to round out the pregame moves for the Commanders.
