stories.title: Giants ‘working through’ quarterback decision, won’t make one yet
stories.summary: John Harbaugh not ready to choose between Jameis winston, J.J. McCarthy
stories.detailText: Jameis Winston and J.J McCarthy | Getty Images New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said on Monday afternoon that the Giants have not yet made a decision who their starting starting quarterback will be on Sunday against the Houston Texans. “We’re working through that now. Honing in on a decision,” Harbaugh said via Zoom. The Giants, of course, have a decision to make after J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and led the Giants from a34-10 deficit to the brink of a stunning comeback on Sunday in a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. What will the decision be based on? “Absolutely like every other personnel decision we make what gives us the best chance to win the football game at this given time or what combination of players and schemes and things like that give us the best chance to, in this case, move the ball, score points, protect the football, etc.,” Harbaugh said. “The things that help us win. Whatever it is that furthers us and helps us. That’s what we want to do.” The Giants are without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart after he suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2. Winston took over as the starter in Week 3, and has gone 2-1-1. McCarthy was acquired Sept. 28 from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a fifth-round pick. “Jameis has done a great job in so many ways. I just admire him and respect him for it,” Harbaugh said. “He’s helped us win games. Did what he had to do to win games, and that’s something you value very much. “J.J. just got here a couple weeks ago. Where do we stand? We’re trying to put an offense together that he’s got a feel for and those kind of things. All those things are things you factor in.” Harbaugh admitted that being without Dart is an ongoing adjustment. “When we lost Jaxson that made it tough for us to be what we said we wanted to be,” Harbaugh said. “That changed everything. We were trying to find ourselves for a few weeks. We still have been, honestly. “The thing that’s important to remember — we are a work in progress. We are most definitely a work in progress … it’s a long season and we are in the midst of it. We are in position. It’s our responsibility now to find ourselves and put together the type of football team and go get what we want. It’s all right there for us.” Harbaugh just isn’t ready to let the world know which quarterback will try to take the Giants where they want to go.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images A long-awaited reunion game will not occur Sunday. The Los Angeles Rams announced that starting wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring in a loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday and he will miss the next 6-10 weeks. The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. The Raiders traded Adams to the New York Jets in 2024 after he requested to be traded from the team he worked to join in 2022. The Raiders sent a first and second round pick to the Green Bay Packers for Adams in 2022 to reunite him with Fresno State teammate Derek Carr. Adams played well for the Raiders, but his relationship with the franchise soured after Carr was released after the 2022 season. Adams, who turns 34 in December, in his second season with the Rams. The Rams are battered. They will also be without defensive tackles Poona Ford and Kobie Turner.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two things can be true about the Las Vegas Raiders’ 3-3 start to the 2026 season. One, the Raiders are playing better than expected, where the rebuild is at least on pace and may even be slightly ahead of schedule. Two, after starting 3-0, dropping three games in a row against legitimate AFC playoff contenders is disappointing and makes any postseason hopes feel like more of a pipe dream than a reality this fall. Las Vegas was at least competitive in a three-point loss to the Buffalo Bills, giving room for optimism when it comes to the Week 6 winners and losers. But, at the same time, there are still plenty of holes to patch up, starting with a few offseason free agent signings. LOSER: Tyler Linderbaum To be clear, Linderbaum hasn’t been “bad” this season and by no means should be replaced in the starting lineup. But the Raiders didn’t make him the highest-paid center in NFL history by $9 million a year to be Pro Football Focus’ 22nd-ranked center with a 58.8 grade through the first six weeks of the campaign. Sunday was an especially bad outing, as he looked outmatched against Bills’ defensive tackle Deone Walker, posting a season-low 46.8 mark . “I didn’t feel good about it,” Linderbaum replied when asked about his Week 6 performance, via Raider Nation Radio on X/Twitter . “I let 96 (Walker) dictate the game one me. Great player, credit to him, he came out ready to play. I’ve just got to play better for the team. [The Raiders] brought me here to be a great run blocker and a great pass protector; I just feel like I let a lot of my teammates down today.” While Walker is having an excellent season, the free-agent addition is supposed to be a Top 5 center in the NFL. That, plus the massive contract, comes with a higher level of expectations, where he, at least, needs to hold his own against top competition. So far, Linderbaum hasn’t held up his end of the bargain and needs to pick it up over the next 11 games, especially since he was brought in to elevate the rest of the offensive line. He also committed his third penalty on a tush-push play. He needs to clean that up as well. LOSER: Quay Walker For the second week in a row, Walker got picked on in coverage. He was targeted six times and gave up six completions for 76 yards and a touchdown for a perfect 158.3 passer rating. Also, 60 or nearly 80 percent of the yards came after the catch, per PFF . The free-signing is having a good year as a run defender, but he continues to have issues in coverage that opposing offenses have started to exploit. WINNER: Treydan Stukes (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Getty Images" /> It’s hard to find silver linings on a defense that gave up 33 points, but Stukes had an impressive outing after having the worst game of his young career the week before. The rookie was all over the field with nine total tackles (third-most on the team), posting a season-high three “ defensive stops ”, per PFF . That helped him post another personal best with a 74.2 run defense grade, and he was solid in coverage as well. Stukes drew five targets and did allow four completions but for just 17 yards. The one notable reception he gave up was an 11-yard grab to wide receiver Keon Coleman, where the defensive back was in position to contest the catch and just lost at the catch point. So, the four other targets resulted in just six yards and a pass breakup. That’s something the second-round pick can build on moving forward. LOSER: Darien Porter On the other end of the spectrum in the secondary, Las Vegas is struggling to find its second starting cornerback. While Eric Stokes had arguably his best game of the season, Porter might have had his worst. The latter was targeted five times and gave up 59 yards on three completions, while the two incompletions were drops. That led to Hezekiah Masses getting more reps in the second half, who also had issues, drawing a penalty on his lone target. Inconsistency has been the story of Porter’s young career. He’ll look like the best corner on the roster one week and then lay an egg in the next game. At some point, that has to get ironed out if the 2025 third-round pick is going to become a reliable starter moving forward. LOSER: Ashton Jeanty One of the themes for this week’s losers is players who aren’t living up to the billing, and Jeanty falls into that category. Yes, the offensive line leaves something to be desired, but the No. 6 overall pick hasn’t shown that he’s the caliber of back to help overcome issues up front and collect rushing yards over expected (RYOE). This season, he ranks 25th at the position with negative 15.2 RYOE, per Muffed.ai , and is tied for 26th in missed tackles forced with nine, according to PFF . The latter was especially bad on Sunday, as Jeanty failed to record a single MTF. That’s understandable if he’s dealing with an injury. But, at the same time, if a bum ankle and/or foot are causing him to be ineffective on the field, then it’s time to sit and heal up. On top of that, the Boise State product dropped his fifth pass of the season and second in as many weeks. It’s time to increase Mike Washington Jr.’s and Dylan Laube’s workloads because Jeanty simply isn’t getting it done right now. WINNER: Michael Mayer (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Getty Images" /> On a more positive note, Mayer continues to have a career season after getting an early contract extension. His seven catches for 95 yards tie for the third-most and the most he’s had in a single game. Also, the fourth-year pro is seven catches and 62 yards away from setting personal bests in both metrics for an entire season, and there are still 11 games left to play. Mayer did a lot of work after the catch against the Bills, recording 67 yards — or over 70 percent of his total — with the ball in his hands. That gives him 158 YAC on the season and puts him second behind Travis Kelce (196) for the most among tight ends, per PFF . WINNER: Tre Tucker Las Vegas’ wide receiver room has been a big talking point during the 2026 campaign, with many waiting for someone in the position group to step up and be productive. With Brock Bowers not having the same impact on Sunday as the Raiders have come to expect over the last month, the fourth-year wideout stepped up and led the team with five catches for 97 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Among the scores was an explosive 44-yarder that cut the fourth-quarter deficit to three points, giving the Silver and Black a chance to tie or win the game after a successful onside kick. The latter didn’t happen, but Tucker did his part to put the opportunity on the table. LOSER: Defensive Tackles It’s no secret that the Raiders’ defensive tackles leave a lot to be desired. But it feels like the Bills game was another reminder of just how big an issue that position group is. Running back James Cook III had 22 carries for 95 yards (4.3 ypc) and a touchdown, and a lot of his production came from runs that were right up the gut. Meanwhile, Adam Butler led the Raiders’ DTs with a 60.4 PFF run defense grade , just 0.4 points above the baseline. The defense is clearly missing a gap filler in the middle of the trenches right now. Perhaps getting Tonka Hemingway back from a concussion this week will help.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Those inside Allegiant Stadium on Sunday afternoon were treated to an old-fashioned third-quarter magic show as Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills offense pulled a rabbit out of their hat on a wild touchdown toss in the red zone. The dazzling display of never giving up on a play resulted in the Bills quarterback Josh Allen flicking the ball to wide receiver Keon Coleman for the 12-yard score to vault Buffalo’s led to 23-16 — an advantage it would hold the rest of the way — highlighting the visitors resilience while also showcasing the host Las Vegas Raiders’ lack of coaching and player execution on defense as the Silver & Black fell 33-30. Las Vegas didn’t go away quietly, however, finally going with deep throws culminating in wide receiver Tre Tucker’s 44-yard diving touchdown catch on a throw from quarterback Kirk Cousins, but the onside drop kick went way too high with Buffalo kneeling the ball to run out the clock. Credit to the Raiders for keeping it close. The team put forth a better effort in a three-point loss than the shellacking in New England in Week 5. However, close isn’t good enough in the NFL and valiant showings don’t necessarily reflect in the final score — and more importantly, the standings — as Klint Kubiak’s Raiders have dropped three-straight games after Sunday’s defeat. “I just want to say very disappointed. Very disappointed that we didn’t get it done today,” Kubiak began his postgame press conference. “Credit to Buffalo; they played a great game. As a team, we did not close the game, and there’s plenty of improvement. But we are not satisfied with any moral victories, and we’re a 3-3 football team with everything ahead of us. Avoided injuries today, so we’re moving forward, but we didn’t get it done today.” lol. pic.twitter.com/afZJM11h7D — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 18, 2026 Forgive Kubiak if the moral victories portion of his presser opener stings a bit. He’s not steeped in the Raiders’ patented ineptitude as many long-time fans are. And for those ardent folks in Raider Nation — buried underneath a mountainous pile of losing the team has done — “close” and “almost” are gargantuan leaps to what they’ve had to bear witness too. Kubiak’s standard is way higher, but the constant pummeling the loyal fanbase has taken, the miniscule crumb that’s the slightest glimmer of hope is a five-course meal for the famished. That noted, it’s difficult to not feel Kubiak’s disappointment. Throughout the game, the Raiders briefly took a lead and tied the contest against a high-octane Bills defense. But miscues in all three phases of the game haunted Las Vegas even when its red zone defense stymied Buffalo. Joe Brady’s Bills offense went 3-of-5 in the red zone while Kubiak’s attack went 2-of-5 and having just one more end zone visit in the area between the opponent’s 20-yard line and goal line was a big difference. As was the lone turnover of the contest, committed by the Raiders. Which makes the mistakes in a variety of aspects — on offense, center Tyler Linderbaum’s false start on 4th-and-short; on defense, eye violations that left Allen and running back James Cook open for a 29-yard catch and run on 3rd-and-3 in the 4th quarter (led to touchdown); on special teams a facemask penalty on Segun Olubi on a punt return — highlight bad complementary football stand out for the Raiders. And the third quarter duds from Las Vegas offense only compounds matters. “It’s happened three times, and it’s killing us, absolutely killing us, and I have not fixed it. So, shame on me. It’s on me to get it fixed,” Kubiak said of Linderbaum’s false start and penchant to do so in short-yardage situations. “I’m really upset with how we’re starting the third quarter. Go three and out. That’s disappointing,” Kubiak added about the team’s third stanza performance. “Every game has adversity. The game’s not over in the third quarter when you go three and out, but it really kills more than that.” The Raiders didn’t get dog walked in Week 6 like it did in Week 5, so progress is being made. And like previous games, there’s plenty of teach tape for coaches and players to pour over and correct as the team preps for Week 7. "WHOAAAAA" "Incredible!" Kirk Cousins to Tre Tucker had Jim & @JJWatt fired up 🚀 @Raiders pic.twitter.com/yGaFa5YZvC — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Tucker torched the Bills secondary on his fourth-quarter touchdown: —Tremendous credit to and effort by Bills cornerback Christian Benford who was tasked quite often with one-on-one coverage on Raiders elite pass catcher Brock Bowers. Benford won more matchups than he lost against Bowers and when Buffalo didn’t have their top corner on Las Vegas’ tight end, Bowers hauled in back-to-back 18- and 29-yard passes on the Raiders’ nine-play, 91-yard fourth-quarter touchdown drive to tie the game at 23. —Both Tucker and tight end Michael Mayer came close to eclipsing the 100-yard receiving mark with 97 and 95, respectively. The fleet-footed wide receiver hauled in five passes and two touchdowns on seven targets while the tight end caught seven passes on nine targets. —Cousins finished 23 of 41 for 313 yards and two touchdown passes with one awful interception. He did avoid getting sacked but took a few hits from Buffalo’s defense. His counterpart, Allen, finished 23 of 33 for 255 yards and two touchdown passes. He was sacked twice. —Raiders defensive end Kwity Paye finally got back in the sack column with his takedown of Allen. Linebacker Quay Walker collected the team’s other sack on a perfectly called blitz in the first quarter. But overall, it was an up-and-down performance from the unit. —The kickers for both teams got plenty of work in this contest as Buffalo’s Tyler Bass went 4-for-4 on field goals with a long of 47. Las Vegas’ Matt Gay finished 3-for-3 with a long of 35. Raiders punter AJ Cole III ended up with three punts for 166 yards (55.3 yards per boot average) with one dropping inside the Bills’ 20-yard line (long of 57). Quote of Note “Yeah, there’s no doubt that, that’s what it is. We got to find ways to close. You got to find the inches in the fourth quarter. You can’t go out in second to last possession and have three incompletions. You can’t in the third quarter throw an interception that gives them a short field and they get a touchdown off of it. You can’t go two for five in the red zone. You know third and goal, we got to come away with those four point plays and get the touchdown, not the kick in the field goal. Those are all the plays throughout the game that you look back on and you say, it didn’t give us a chance to win.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on what it would take to close games out. I’d be remiss if I didn’t include the comedic moment on the CBS broadcast between JJ Watt and Jim Nantz that I tweeted about : JIM NANTZ JUST TRIED TO PEANUT PUNCH @JJWatt 🤣 "I did not think you were gonna go that hard" "my wrist is broken" 😭 pic.twitter.com/ocdRBn282r — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 Up Next Sitting at .500 at 3-3 overall, the Raiders head to Inglewood for the second time this season, this time to face the Los Angeles Rams next Sunday. The host Rams fell to 2-4 overall after watching Chad Ryland’s 43-yard field goal go through the uprights as time expired as the Arizona Cardinals (also 2-4) got the 18-16 upset win. Las Vegas eyes getting back in the win column after three-straight losses and L.A. is just 1-3 at home this season.
